And at the city of Neocaesarea, the feast of the holy martyrs Martio, Musonius, Eugenius, and Mitellus, who were handed over to the fire; their relics were scattered into the river Axius.

And the feast of the three children Urbanus, Prilidanus, and Eupolonus.

### D. Eighth Day before the Kalends of February

The Conversion of Saint Paul.

On the same day, Saint Ananias at Damascus, who baptized blessed Paul.

At the city of Gabilon, Saint Severianus the bishop, a man of wondrous holiness and learning.

Also the feast of Praejectus, bishop of Auvergne.

And the feast of Saint Gregory the Theologian.

### E. Seventh Day before the Kalends of February

The feast of Saint Polycarp, blessed disciple of the apostle John. Ordained bishop of Smyrna by John, he was the leading bishop of all Asia. After dreadful tortures, he was finally placed in the midst of a pyre and pierced with a sword; so much blood poured forth that it extinguished the fire.

Twelve others who had come from Philadelphia suffered with him. At that time Germanicus also, a distinguished athlete of Christ, was transferred through the glorious contest of martyrdom. When the judge had condemned him to the beasts, he voluntarily challenged the beast prepared for him, scorning temporal death and desiring to attain the crown of eternal life by a swift end.

On the same day, the feast of Saint Theogenes the martyr and six others.

At the city of Bourges, Saint Sulpitius the bishop and confessor.

### F. Sixth Day before the Kalends of February

The feast of Saint John, bishop of Constantinople, surnamed Chrysostom, who greatly benefited the Christian religion by word and example.

Also blessed Maurus, abbot of the monastery of Bobbio.

And at Bethlehem, the falling-asleep of blessed Paula, mother of Eustochium, virgin of Christ. She belonged to a most noble senatorial family, but renounced the world and distributed her wealth among the poor. Having attained the poverty of Christ, she became, near the town mentioned above, the mother of a glorious monastery of virgins at the Lord’s Nativity.

Writing her life, admirable for its virtues, Saint Jerome testifies that she was crowned by a long martyrdom.

And the saints Datus, Julian, Vincent, and twenty-seven others.

### G. Fifth Day before the Kalends of February

The second feast of Saint Agnes.

And in the city of Apollonia, the martyrs Leucius, Thyrsus, and Callinicus, who were tortured by various kinds of torment during the reign of the emperor Decius, under the governors Cumbritius, Silvanus, and Baudius. The first and the last completed their martyrdom by beheading; the one in the middle, summoned by a heavenly voice, gave up his spirit, and they rested in Christ.

At Alexandria, blessed Cyril the bishop, who proved himself a most distinguished defender of the Catholic faith.

And in the monastery of Leomana, John the presbyter, a man of God.

### A. Fourth day before the Kalends of February

At Rome, the feast of Papias and Maurus, soldiers under Diocletian. When they saw the steadfastness of the martyrs Saturninus and Sisinius, they were converted to the faith. Immediately Laodicius, prefect of the city, ordered that the mouths of those who confessed Christ be battered with stones and that they be thrust into prison. There they were baptized by blessed Pope Marcellus. After twelve days he ordered them brought out, stretched upon the ground, and beaten with clubs; then, lifted from the ground, they were beaten with leaden weights until they expired. The priest John gathered their bodies by night and buried them on the Nomentan Way, at the nymphs of blessed Peter, where he was baptizing. [Col. 0827B] This is written in the Acts of blessed Pope Marcellus.

At Trier, the burial of blessed Valerius, bishop and disciple of the holy apostle Peter.

### B. Third day before the Kalends of February

At Antioch, the passion of Saint Hippolytus. For a time he had been somewhat deceived by the schism of Novatian, but, through the working of Christ’s grace, he was corrected and returned to the charity of the Church; for its sake, and within it, he later completed a glorious martyrdom.

At Jerusalem, blessed Matthias, bishop, concerning whom wondrous and faith-filled deeds are related. After suffering many things for Christ, he finally ended his life in peace; he governed the Church as the eighth bishop after James. [Col. 0828A]

Also, blessed Alexander. During the persecution of Decius he was brought before tribunals for his confession of the faith and handed over to prison bonds. Though he shone with the venerable white hair of advanced age, and had frequently glorified the Lord through his sufferings, he was repeatedly led from his bonds to the tribunals and from the tribunals back to his bonds. Amid these tortures, which succeeded one another in turn, he rested in a blessed end.

At the monastery of Albodium, the feast of Aldegund, a virgin. Born of noble lineage in the time of Dagobert, king of the Franks, she chose the purpose of virginity and remained steadfast in it. An angelic vision was often revealed to her, exhorting her to persevere in her purpose; finally, with great brilliance of heavenly light, she departed to life. [Col. 0828B]

### C. The day before the Kalends of February

At Alexandria, the feast of Saint Methranus, martyr. The pagans seized him and ordered him to utter impious words. [Col. 0829A] When he refused, they battered his whole body with clubs, pierced his face and eyes with sharpened reeds, and drove him outside the city amid tortures. There, what remained of his spirit they expelled with stones. [Col. 0830A]

Also, Saturninus, Thyrsus, and Victor; and, at the city of Trent, blessed Vigilius, bishop and martyr; and the feast of Saints Rarsus, Zoticus, Ammoninus, and Publius.

### February

February has twenty-eight days and twenty-nine lunar days; in a leap year it has twenty-nine days.

[Col. 0829B]

### D. Kalends of February

At Antioch, the passion of Saint Ignatius, bishop and martyr.

At Smyrna, Saint Pionius, martyr. During the persecution of Antoninus Verus, after displaying unconquerable steadfastness in his replies and enduring the squalor of prison, where by his exhortations he strengthened many of the brethren to endure martyrdom, he was finally afflicted with many tortures, fastened with nails, and placed upon a burning pyre. [Col. 0829C] Thus he obtained a blessed end of life for Christ. Fifteen others suffered with him. [Col. 0830B]

On the same day, blessed Ephrem, deacon of the church of Edessa.

In Scotland, Saint Brigid, virgin, whose life was renowned for miracles. When she touched a piece of altar wood as a testimony to her virginity, it became green.

And the feast of Saint Paul, bishop of the city of Troyes, whose life shone with virtues and whose precious death is commended by miracles. [Col. 0830C]

In Greece, Saint Polycarp, bishop; and at Ravenna, Saint Severus, bishop.

[Col. 0831A]

### E. Fourth day before the Nones of February

The Purification of Saint Mary, when she was presented in the temple with the infant.

At Caesarea, blessed Cornelius the centurion, whom blessed Peter baptized and who, raised to episcopal dignity in that city, fell asleep in peace.

At Rome, Saint Apronianus, martyr. During the persecution of the emperor Maximian, when he had brought before the eyes of Laodicius the prefect the blessed deacon Sisinius, led out of prison—for Apronianus was a prison clerk—and had suddenly seen a light appear and heard a voice at the same time, he fell trembling at the feet of the deacon Sisinius and said: [Col. 0832A]

“I adjure you by Christ whom you confess: do not delay to baptize me, and make me attain the crown.”

Blessed Sisinius baptized him and brought him to Pope Marcellus to be sealed with sacred chrism. When the prefect learned of this, he ordered him to undergo the capital sentence. He was therefore led to the second milestone on the Salarian Way and beheaded; he departed as a martyr and victor.

At Orléans, the burial of Siccaria, a virgin consecrated to God.

At the Forum of Sempronius, Saints Laurentius and Hippolytus, and the feast of Saint Fortunatus.

### F. Third day before the Nones of February

At Sebaste, a city of Cappadocia, the passion of Saint Blaise, bishop and martyr of Christ. Under the governor Agricola, he was beheaded [Col. 0833A] together with two little boys, sons of one of the seven women who had been strengthened by his preaching and martyred under the same governor.

At Lyon, the burial of blessed Lupicinus, bishop.

At Vienne, Saint Eventius, glorious bishop.

In Africa, blessed Celerinus, deacon and confessor; and the holy martyrs Celerina, his grandmother, and Laurentinus and Ignatius. The first was his paternal uncle, the second his maternal uncle. A letter of blessed Cyprian exists concerning the glorious praise of all of them.

[Col. 0834A]

### G. The day before the Nones of February

In the Egyptian city called Thmuis, the passion of blessed Phileas, bishop of that city, and of Philoromus, a tribune of the Roman soldiers. With them, an innumerable multitude of the faithful from the same city, following the footsteps of their shepherd during the persecution of Diocletian, was crowned with martyrdom.

At the Forum of Symphronius, the feast of Gemini, Gelasius, Mammius, Aquilinus, and Donatus.

Also, Themoi and Gelasius.

### A. The Nones of February

At Patras, the ordination of the episcopate of Saint Andrew the apostle.

In Sicily, at the city of the people of Catania, the passion of Saint Agatha, virgin, under the consul Quintianus in the time of Diocletian. [Col. 0835A] After blows and imprisonment, after the rack and tortures, after the cutting off of her breasts—but their healing by the Lord—after being rolled over potsherds and coals, she finally completed her martyrdom in prison.

At Vienne, blessed Avitus, bishop, through whose faith, diligence, and wondrous teaching, in the time of King Gundobad, Gaul was defended from the assault of the Arian heresy; and Saints Felix, Fortunatus, and Saturninus.

### B. Eighth day before the Ides of February

At Rome, on the Appian Way, in the cemetery of the same name, the passion of Saint Soter, virgin.

At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the feast of Saint Dorothea, virgin, and Theophilus, under the prefect Apricius. Dorothea had been entrusted to two sisters, Christa and Callista, who had recently apostatized from the faith. [Col. 0835B] They were overcome by sufferings in order to turn her away from Christ, but she converted them again to Christ, so that when the prefect had them thrown into a vat and burned, they attained the palm of martyrdom. [Col. 0836A]

Afterward Dorothea was led to the place of punishment, where she also suffered. A certain scholar named Theophilus mocked her because, as she was going to paradise, she had said that her bridegroom Christ would send him roses and apples. She immediately promised that she would send them.

When they had arrived at the place where she was to be slaughtered, she prayed for a little while, then brought out her scarf and called to her a certain boy of six years. She sent him to Theophilus, saying:

“Tell him that Dorothea, the handmaid of God, sends you apples from the paradise of her bridegroom Christ.”

He received them and gave thanks because she had fulfilled his request. Then he began to wipe his face, and suddenly he was filled with such sweetness that his whole mind was changed. [Col. 0836B] With great rejoicing and a loud voice he repeatedly exclaimed: [Col. 0837A]

“Blessed is the name of my Lord Jesus Christ!”

For this confession he too was immediately seized and hung upon the rack. He was tortured with such cruelty that all who stood around were horrified. Finally, his head was struck off, and he completed his martyrdom.

At the city of Arverna, the feast of Saint Anatolius, martyr.

In Gaul, at the city of Aderato, the burial of Saint Vedastus, bishop and confessor.

At the monastery of Ellone, the burial of Saint Amandus, bishop and confessor.

At Rome, Zoticus, Irenaeus, Hyacinthus, and Amantius.

In the East, Saint Soter, virgin. After being severely and very long beaten with blows, and after overcoming a hundred kinds of punishment, she completed her martyrdom by the sword.

### C. Seventh day before the Ides of February

In Britain, at the city of Augusta, the feast of Saint Augulus, bishop and martyr; and of Saint Moysetes, venerable bishop. [Col. 0837B] At first he led a solitary life in the desert and became greatly renowned through the merits, virtues, and signs that God performed through him. Later, at the request of Manvia, queen of the Saracens, he became bishop of that people. He preserved the fellowship of the Catholic faith undefiled and converted a large part of the people over whom he had been appointed bishop to the faith of Christ. Thus he rested in peace.

### D. Sixth day before the Ides of February

At Rome, the feast of Saint Paul, bishop, and of Julius, pope. [Col. 0838A]

In Lesser Armenia, the feast of Saints Dionysius, Aemilianus, and Sebastian.

At Alexandria, the feast of Saint Cointha, martyr. The pagans seized her and led her to the idols, forcing her to worship. When she cursed and refused them, they fastened chains to her feet and dragged her through the streets of the entire city, tearing her apart in a horrifying punishment.

And Saint Helena, queen.

### E. Fifth day before the Ides of February

At Alexandria, Saint Apollonia, virgin. The persecutors first knocked out all her teeth. Then they built and lit a pyre and threatened to burn her alive unless she uttered impious words with them. When she saw that the pyre had been kindled, she deliberated briefly within herself, suddenly broke free from the hands of the impious, and voluntarily leapt into the fire they had prepared. [Col. 0838B] Even the authors of the cruelty were terrified, because the woman proved readier for death than the persecutor for punishment.

At Suevo, in Cyprus, the feast of Saint Alexander and Ammonius.

Also, Ammonius and thirty-eight others.

### F. Fourth day before the Ides of February

In Campania, the feast of Saint Silvanus, bishop and confessor.

In Bethlehem of Judaea, under King Herod, the passion of Saint Andrew the apostle.

At the city of Sancton, the burial of Saint Trojan, bishop and confessor, and of Baldegund, abbess. [Col. 0839A]

At Rome, on the Lavican Way, ten soldiers; and the burial of Saint Scholastica, virgin.

### G. Third day before the Ides of February

At Rome, Calocerius and Parthenius.

At Lyon, Saint Desiderius, bishop and martyr.

At Vienne, Saint Simplicius, bishop and confessor.

Also at Alexandria, the burial of Euphrosina, virgin, who shone in the monastery through wondrous strength of abstinence and through miracles.

### A. The day before the Ides of February

In Spain, at the city of Barcelona, the feast of Saint Eulalia, virgin, who suffered in the time of the emperor Diocletian under Datianus, prefect of Spain. At the same time, at Barcelona Saint Cuxupas and at Gerunda Saint Felix are likewise known to have received glorious crowns of martyrdom. [Col. 0839B]

In Africa, the passion of Saint Damian, soldier.

At Alexandria, Modestus and Ammonius, children; and the burial of Simplicius, bishop and confessor.

### B. Ides of February

At Antioch, the feast of Agabus the prophet, of whom blessed Luke writes in the Acts of the Apostles. [Col. 0840A]

In the Armenian city of Militene, the feast of Saint Polyeuctus, martyr, whose name is interpreted in Latin as “one who prays much.”

And the feast of Saint Gregory, pope, who governed the Church for sixteen years in the time of the emperors Leo and Constantine. He was a chaste man and learned in the divine Scriptures. Through Boniface, bishop, he preached the word of salvation in Germany. During Lent he established that the fast and celebration of Mass should take place on Thursday, which had not previously been done.

At Lyon, the burial of blessed Stephen, bishop.

### C. Sixteenth day before the Kalends of March

At Rome, the feast of Saint Valentine, priest. After many signs of healing and teaching, he was beaten with clubs and then beheaded under Caesar Claudius.

On the same day, the feast of Saint Valentine, bishop of Interamna. Seized by the pagans and beaten with rods, he was handed over to custody after a prolonged beating. When he could not be overcome, he was thrown out of prison in the silence of midnight and beheaded at the order of the furious Placidus, prefect of the city.

Then Proculus, Ephibus, and Apollonius, his disciples, carried his body [Col. 0841A] to their church in Interamna and buried it by night. While they kept daily vigils there, they were seized by the pagans and handed over to the custody of the consul Leontius. He ordered them to be brought before his tribunal in the middle of the night. When they could not be recalled from the faith either by entreaties or threats, he ordered them to be beheaded. They were buried not far from the body of Saint Valentine.

On the same day, the holy martyrs Vitalis, Felicula, and Zeno.

At Alexandria, Saints Bassus, Antonius, and Protolichus, who were drowned in the sea.

Also, Cyrion, priest; Moses; Bassianus, lector; and Agatho, exorcist, all of whom were burned in fire.

Also, Dionysius and Ammonius, who were beheaded.

### D. Fifteenth day before the Kalends of March

At Rome, Saint Craton, martyr. [Col. 0842A] He had a scholarly son named Cheremon who fell into a very serious illness. Craton brought him to blessed Valentine, bishop, to be healed, on the condition that if the boy were healed, Craton himself and his entire household would become Christians. When the boy was healed, he fulfilled what he had promised. He was baptized with his wife and the whole household and, not many days afterward, completed his martyrdom.

In Gaul, at the city of Vaison, the burial of Quinctius, bishop, whose death is attested as precious in the sight of the Lord by frequent miracles.

At Antioch, the feast of Joseph, deacon, and Zeno.

At Interamna, the feast of Agape, virgin, Saturninus, and Castula.

At the city of Prexia, Saints Faustinus and Jonita, martyrs.

[Col. 0843A]

### E. Fourteenth day before the Kalends of March

The feast of Saint Onesimus the apostle, concerning whom blessed Paul the apostle sends a familiar letter to Philemon. The same blessed apostle ordained him bishop and entrusted to him the word of preaching, then left him at the city of Ephesus, where he himself served as bishop after blessed Timothy. He was brought to Rome and there stoned for the faith of Christ. He was first buried there as a martyr of Christ; afterward his body was transferred to the place where he had been ordained bishop.

At Cumae, the feast of Saint Juliana, virgin. In the time of the emperor Maximian, she was first beaten and severely tortured by her father, Africanus. Then the prefect Eleusius, to whom she had been betrothed, had her stripped, beaten with rods, suspended by her hair, and covered over the head with molten lead. She was then returned to prison, [Col. 0843B] where she openly fought with the devil. Again brought out, she overcame the torments of wheels, flames, and a boiling cauldron, [Col. 0844A] and completed her martyrdom by beheading.

She suffered at Nicomedia but, after a short time, was transferred by God’s providence to Campania.

In Egypt, Julianus and five thousand others.

### F. Thirteenth day before the Kalends of March

In Babylonia, the feast of Polychronius, bishop of that city. In the presence of the persecutor Decius, after his mouth had been beaten with stones, he stretched out his hands, raised his eyes to heaven, and gave up his spirit.

This is written in the Passion of Saint Laurence.

### G. Twelfth day before the Kalends of March

At Jerusalem, blessed Symeon, bishop and martyr, who is said to have been related to the Savior according to the flesh. It is nevertheless established that Cleophas, whose son he was, was the brother of Joseph. [Col. 0844B]

On the same day, the holy martyrs Claudius and his wife Praepedigna, their sons Alexander and Cutia, and Claudius’s brother, blessed Maximus. [Col. 0845A] Since they were of the most distinguished lineage, they were baptized by blessed Gaius, Roman pontiff, through the agency of their brother Gabinius, a priest. Later, by order of Diocletian, they were seized by the impious judge Julius. Claudius, together with his wife and sons, was deported into exile; afterward they were burned in a fire and offered God the fragrant sacrifice of martyrdom. Later they were thrown into the sea at Ostia, and Christians searched for their relics and buried them near the city.

### A. Eleventh day before the Kalends of March

At Rome, Saint Gabinius, priest, father of the most blessed Susanna. After being afflicted for a long time in custody and chains by Diocletian, he obtained the joys of heaven through a precious death.

In Africa, the feast of Saints Publius, Julianus, and Marubius. [Col. 0845B]

Also, Julianus, Marcellus, Tullus, Lampasius, and Inaulus.

### B. Tenth day before the Kalends of March

At Rome, the feast of Gaius, pope.

In Cyprus, the feast of Potamia, Nemesius, and Didymus; and elsewhere, of Victor, a martyr, Corona, and twenty others. [Col. 0846A]

At Tyre, the greatest city of Phoenicia, the feast of blessed martyrs whose number is known only to God. At the command of Diocletian, Veturius, master of the soldiers, killed them through various kinds of torture, each following upon the other. First the martyrs of God were torn throughout their bodies with whips. After this they were handed over to beasts: lions, bears, leopards, boars, and bulls were brought against them. Yet none of these animals injured them. Finally, with swords, the executioners accomplished what the beasts had been unable to do.

They were led by the bishops Tyrannio and Sylvanus, who afterward completed their martyrdom through the bites of beasts. The bishops Pelenus and Linus, with many clerics, were consumed by fire. The priest Zenobius was beheaded.

### C. Ninth day before the Kalends of March

In Africa, the feast of Saints Verolus, Servolus, Secundinus, Siricius, Felix, Saturninus, Fortunatus, and sixteen others. [Col. 0846B]

And the burial of Eucherius, bishop.

In Sicily, seventy-nine holy martyrs who, under Diocletian, amid various tortures, were deemed worthy to receive from Christ the crown prepared for their confession. [Col. 0847A]

### D. Eighth day before the Kalends of March

The Chair of Saint Peter, who sat at Antioch, where the disciples were first called Christians.

At Alexandria, Abilius, bishop, who was the second bishop after blessed Mark and served in the priesthood for thirteen years.

At Hierapolis, Saint Papias, bishop and hearer of the apostle John.

At Vienne, Saint Paschasius, bishop and confessor.

Also, blessed Aristion, who was one of Christ’s seventy-two disciples.

At Nicomedia, the feast of Saint Thecla, virgin, disciple of the apostle Paul. Under the emperor Nero she was handed over to fire for the name of Christ, but was not burned. Later she was given over to serpents and beasts, but was injured by none of them. Finally, at Seleucia, she departed to the Lord through the sleep of peace, with the martyrdom of her virginity and the honor of her virtues. [Col. 0847B]

At Rome, on the Tiburtine Way, at Saint Laurence, the feast of Saint Concordia, whom the persecution of Decius slaughtered.

### E. Seventh day before the Kalends of March

In Pannonia, the feast of Saints Seronetus, Antigonus, Rutulus, and Libus. [Col. 0848A]

On the same day, Saint Polycarp, priest and confessor, who converted very many people to the faith of Christ together with blessed Sebastian and, by exhorting them, led them to the glory of martyrdom.

At Sirmium, the feast of Saint Syrenus, monk. In the time of the emperor Maximian, one of the emperor’s household brought his wife into the garden that Syrenus himself cultivated and walked with her there at an unsuitable hour. Syrenus rebuked her sharply and drove her away. By Maximian’s order he was seized, confessed himself to be a Christian, and was beheaded.

Also, sixty-two others who suffered there.

And the vigil of the apostle Matthias.

### F. Sixth day before the Kalends of March

The feast of Saint Matthias the apostle, who was chosen by the apostles from among the seventy disciples to replace Judas the betrayer and, selected by lot for the apostleship, preached the Gospel of Christ in Judaea.

And the discovery of the head of the Forerunner in the time of the emperor Marcian. The Forerunner himself appeared to two monks and ordered them to go to the former dwelling of King Herod, seek his head there, [Col. 0848B] and rebury it with due honor. [Col. 0849A] They found and took it, but not long afterward it was lost through their negligent care. Others carried it to Emessa, where it was ignobly hidden for a considerable time in an urn beneath the ground in a certain cave. Eventually it revealed itself, and its head, to a religious priest named Marcellus while he was living in that cave.

From that time, in the same city, the beheading of the blessed Forerunner began to be celebrated on the very day on which his head had been found or raised up.

At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the feast of blessed Sergius, martyr, whose illustrious deeds are recorded.

### G. Fifth day before the Kalends of March

In Egypt, the feast of Saints Victorinus, Victor, Nicephorus, Claudianus, Dioscorus, Serapion, and Papias under Numerian, with Sabinus serving as commander.

The first was placed in a hollow wooden ball pierced through on every side and was pierced for a very long time through each opening. [Col. 0849B] When an excessive amount of blood flowed out, he was taken from the ball and beheaded.

The second, after his hands and feet had been cut off, was placed in the same ball, endured the tortures of the first, and was finally struck with a sword.

The third entered the ball voluntarily. The indignant judge ordered him brought out and roasted for a while on a grate laid over burning coals, turning him from side to side. When he persisted in his confession, he was taken away, cut into pieces with a sword, and gave up his spirit.

Of the remaining four, Claudianus and Dioscorus were burned in flames; Serapion and Papias completed their martyrdom by the sword.

In Africa, the feast of Saints Donatus, Justus, Rotulus, Herena, Pision, Pamphilus, Nestor, and Casta, and of Saint Walpurga, virgin. [Col. 0850A]

### A. Fourth day before the Kalends of March

At the city of Perge in Pamphylia, the feast of Saint Nestor, bishop. During the persecution of Decius, he devoted himself day and night to prayer, asking that the flock of Christ be guarded. He was arrested by a certain Irenarchus, chief officer of the city, and brought before the governor Pollio.

When he confessed the name of Christ and declared the gods of the pagans to be demons, the governor ordered him to be tortured with extreme cruelty. Astonished at his endurance, the governor said to him:

“Do you wish to be with us, or with your Christ?”

Saint Nestor replied with great joy:

“With my Christ I was, with him I am, and with him I shall be.”

Then the governor dictated the sentence: whoever confessed the crucified Christ was to be crucified and, as one devoted to his God, released from life. [Col. 0850B]

Giving thanks to God, Nestor, already fastened to the cross, taught the Christian people to persevere in the faith. After this he asked everyone to bend their knees and pray with him. When the prayer was completed and all had said “Amen,” he gave up his spirit.

On the same day, blessed Alexander, bishop of the city of Alexandria, a glorious old man. After blessed Peter, he expelled his own presbyter Arius from the Church because he had been corrupted by heretical impiety and had joined himself to divine truth.

Also, Saints Theon, Opion, Justus, Donatus, Ampliatus, and Ingenius.

### B. Third day before the Kalends of March

In Spain, at the city of Seville, the feast of Saint Leander, bishop. Blessed Gregory wrote the books of the *Moralia* to him. [Col. 0851A] Through his preaching and diligence, the entire nation of the Visigoths was converted from Arian impiety.

On the same day, at Alexandria, the feast of Saint Julianus, martyr. He was so crippled by gout that he could neither walk nor stand, and was brought before the judge in a small chair together with those who carried him. One denied; the other, named Eunus, persevered with the old Julianus in the confession of Christ.

By order of the judge they were placed upon camels, led around the whole city, and torn with whips from every side in the sight of the people, until they met their end through the very blows.

At Lyon, Saint Baldimer, man of God. [Col. 0852A]

At Thessalonica, the feast of Alexander, Androgonus, and Abundantius.

In Africa, Dionysius and twenty-four others.

### C. The day before the Kalends of March

In the green places of the territory of Lyon, blessed Romanus, abbot, who first led an eremitical life there and, renowned for many virtues and miracles, later became the father of many monks. His venerable body was laid to rest in the territory of Besançon.

At Alexandria, the holy martyrs Cerealis, Pupulus, Gaius, and Serapion.

### March

March has thirty-one days and thirty lunar days.

[Col. 0851B]

### D. Kalends of March

At Angers, the burial of Saint Alban, bishop.

At Rome, two hundred and sixty holy martyrs in the time of Claudius. They had been condemned for the name of Christ while digging sand on the Salarian Way. Claudius ordered them to be taken to a pottery outside the walls of the Salarian Way [Col. 0851C] and, enclosed there in the city amphitheater, killed by the arrows of soldiers.

On the same day, the burial of Saint Suitbert, bishop and confessor.

### E. Sixth day before the Nones of March

At Rome, on the Latin Way, Saints Jovinus and Basileus, who suffered under the emperors Gallienus and Valerian; and Simplicius, pope, who sat for fifteen years. [Col. 0852B]

He condemned Acacius, bishop of Constantinople, and Peter, bishop of Alexandria, as Eutychians.

On the same day, many martyrs who suffered under the emperor Alexander. After torturing them for a long time, the impious Alexander condemned them to death at the end. [Col. 0852C]

At Caesarea in Cappadocia, Luke, bishop.

At the Roman Port, Paul, Secundola, Januaria, and Saints Lorgius, Herglius, and Absalon.

### F. Fifth day before the Nones of March

The feast of the holy martyrs Emeterius and Celedonius. They were soldiers in the city of León in Galatia. When the storm of persecution arose, they were subjected to many tortures for confessing the name of Christ, brought as far as Calahorra, and crowned there with martyrdom. [Col. 0853A]

When the executioners cut off their heads, a great miracle appeared to the people. For the ring of one and the scarf of the other were caught up by a cloud and carried into the heavens. Everyone present saw this. As far as their eyes could follow, they watched in astonishment the gleam of gold and the whiteness of the linen.

Aurelianus Clemens records this in the book *Coronatorum* (“The Crowned”).

At Caesarea in Palestine, the holy martyrs Marinus, a soldier, and Asterius, a senator, under the persecution of Valerian. This is written in the *Ecclesiastical History*.

And the feast of Saints Felix, Luciolus, Fortunatus, Marcia, Herod, Antigonus, Januarius, Tutella, Gabianus, and Quirillus; also Felix, Florianus, and Donatus. [Col. 0853B]

### G. Fourth day before the Nones of March

The feast of Saint Lucius, pope and martyr. During the persecution of Valerian and Gallienus, he was sent into exile for the faith of Christ. Later, by divine will, he was permitted to return to his Church, and completed his martyrdom by beheading. He was buried on the Appian Way at Saint Sixtus.

He sat in the episcopate for three years, three months, and three days. He ordered that two priests and three deacons should not leave a bishop in any place, for the sake of ecclesiastical testimony. [Col. 0854A]

Also at Rome, on the Appian Way, nine hundred holy martyrs who were laid in the cemetery at Saint Cecilia.

On the same day, Saint Gaius Palatinus, drowned in the sea.

At Rome, the burial of Julius, bishop, and Nicomedes; and the passion of Saint Adrian with thirty-three others.

### A. Third day before the Nones of March

At Antioch, the passion of Saint Phocas, martyr. After suffering many insults for the name of the Redeemer, the manner in which he triumphed over that ancient serpent is still displayed to the people today. Indeed, if a serpent should bite someone and pour out its venom, the person who has been struck is immediately healed when, trusting in the martyr, he touches the door of his basilica; the power of the poison is removed.

Also on the same day, Saint Eusebius Palatinus and nine other martyrs.

### B. The day before the Nones of March

At Nicomedia, the feast of Saints Victor and Victorinus. For three years they were afflicted with tortures together with Claudianus and his wife Bassa and were thrust into prison, where they completed the course of their lives.

And the burial of Saint Quiriacus, priest.

### C. Nones of March

In Mauretania, at the city of the people of Tuburbo, the passion of the holy martyrs Perpetua and Felicitas, and with them Revocatus, Saturninus, and Secundulus. The last of these rested in prison; all the others were handed over to the beasts, under the emperor Severus, on the day of his birthday.

While they were still being kept in prison and Felicitas was in labor, the prayers of all the holy fellow soldiers obtained that she should give birth in the eighth month.

Among other things, Perpetua was granted that her mind was, in a certain way, turned away from her body. Thus, when she endured the charge of a cow, she still awaited what was to happen, unaware that it had already happened to her.

### D. Eighth day before the Ides of March

At Carthage, Saint Pontianus, deacon of blessed Cyprian, bishop. He endured exile with him until the day of his passion, left behind an excellent volume of his Life and Passion, and, glorifying the Lord through his sufferings, earned the crown of life. [Col. 0855B]

At Nicomedia, Quintulus, bishop, and Capitulinus.

In Africa, Rogatus, Bera, Herma, Felicitas, Orbanus, Cyril, bishop, Sylvanus, and Mamillus.

### E. Seventh day before the Ides of March

At Sebaste in Lesser Armenia, forty soldiers in the time of King Licinius, under the governor Agricolaus. After repeated bonds and imprisonments and after their faces had been beaten with stones, they were thrown into a lake. [Col. 0856A] There the ice-bound bodies were split apart during the night, and in the morning they completed their martyrdom through the breaking of their legs.

Their bodies were then burned and thrown into a river. Yet by divine providence their relics were found intact and buried with due honor.

The more distinguished among them were Quirion and Candidus. The names of the others were: Domitianus, Eunoicus, Sisinius, Heraclius, Alexander, John, Claudius, Athanasius, Valens, Helianus, Melion, Beditas, Achacius, Jubianus, Helius, Theodolus, Cyril, Flavius, Severianus, Cirion, Valerius, Chudion, Sacerdon, Priscus, Euthychius, Smaragdus, Philocimon, Aetius, Micallius, Lysimachus, Domnus, Theophilus, Xantius, Aggius, Leontius, Isitius, Gaius, and Gorgonius.

[Col. 0856B]

### F. Sixth day before the Ides of March

The feast of the holy martyrs Alexander and Gaius of Eumenia, who were crowned with martyrdom at Apamea during the persecution of Antoninus Verus, as Apollinaris of Jerusalem writes in his book *Against the Cataphrygians*.

In Persia, the feast of forty-two holy martyrs.

At Bobbio, the feast of Attala, abbot and confessor.

At Antioch, Agape, virgin, and Mariana.

At Smyrna, Phronis.

At Nicomedia, Palatinus, Firmianus, and Rusticus.

### G. Fifth day before the Ides of March

At the city of Nyssa, Saint Gregory, bishop, brother of blessed Basil of Caesarea, a most learned man and renowned for eloquence. [Col. 0857A]

At Barcelona, Patianus, bishop, distinguished both in life and in speech. He died in an excellent old age during the time of the emperor Theodosius.

At Alexandria, Heraclius, Zosimus, and Alexander.

### A. Fourth day before the Ides of March

At Rome, Saint Gregory, pope, who was a most brilliant teacher in the law of God. Through Augustine, Mellitus, and John, servants of God, he converted the nation of the English to the faith of Christ. He sat there for thirteen years, six months, and ten days.

He added to the prayer of the Canon: “And dispose our days in your peace.”

On the same day, blessed Innocent, pope, who governed the Church for fifteen years, two months, and twenty-one days. He issued a decree concerning the Church and condemned Pelagius and Celestine as heretics. [Col. 0857B] He established that whoever had been born of a Christian woman should be reborn through baptism, a doctrine Pelagius condemned. [Col. 0858A]

At Nicomedia, blessed Peter, martyr, under Diocletian. Because he had protested against the immense tortures inflicted on the holy martyr Noma, he was ordered to be hung and his whole body torn with whips. When his entrails had been laid bare by the stripping away of his skin, vinegar and salt were poured over them. Finally, he ended his life on a grate laid over burning coals.

Also at Nicomedia, the feast of Egdonius, priest, and seven others, who were strangled on successive days in order to strike fear into the rest; and the passion of Maximilian, martyr.

### B. Third day before the Ides of March

At Nicomedia, the feast of Macedonius, priest, and Patricia, his wife, and their daughter Modesta.

At Nicaea, the feast of the holy martyrs Teuseta and Horrius, her son; Theodora, Nymphodora, Marca, and Arabia. [Col. 0858B] All of them were committed to the fire. [Col. 0859A]

Julius, bishop of Alexandria.

### C. The day before the Ides of March

At Rome, the feast of forty-seven martyrs. They were baptized by the apostle Peter while he was being held in the Mamertine prison together with his fellow apostle Paul, where they were detained for nine months. All of them were put to death by Nero’s sword while making a most devoted confession of the faith.

At Carthage, Saints Donatus, Effrosus, and Fruminus.

At Nicomedia, the feast of Felicissimus and Frontina.

### D. Ides of March

In Cappadocia, the passion of Saint Longinus, martyr. In the little book of his martyrdom it is related that, while he was once serving as a soldier under a Roman centurion, he opened the Lord’s side with a lance at the Passion. When he saw the earthquake and the signs that occurred, he believed in Christ and repented of his former deeds. [Col. 0859B]

Afterward he became a monk and served Christ for thirty-eight years, converting many to the faith of God. Finally, he completed his martyrdom in Cappadocia under the governor Octavius. Because of his unbelief, Octavius had been struck by divine judgment with bodily blindness; after his martyrdom, Longinus restored his sight. [Col. 0860A]

At Thessalonica, the feast of Saint Matrona. She was the servant of a certain Jewish woman and secretly worshiped Christ. Discovered by her mistress and beaten until death, she gave back an undefiled spirit.

## E. Seventeenth day before the Kalends of April

At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Cyriacus, who, after the long affliction of imprisonment which he endured under Maximian, together with his fellow deacon Sisinnius and with Smaragdus and Largus, performed many miracles. Among these, at the request of Diocletian himself, he healed Artemia, Diocletian’s daughter, from a demon and baptized her; likewise Jobia, the daughter of Sapor, king of the Persians. Sent there by Diocletian for this purpose, he likewise freed her from a demon and baptized her, together with the king himself and four hundred and thirty others. Returning to Rome [Col. 0860B] after Diocletian’s death, he was arrested among other Christians by his son Maximian and sent into custody because he had made his sister a Christian.

Then Maximian ordered that on the day of his procession Cyriacus should be stripped naked, bound in chains, and dragged before his chariot. After this he was brought out of prison with his companions Largus, Smaragdus, and Crescentianus; through the deputy Carpasianus, his head was drenched with liquefied pitch. Four days later he was again brought out of prison, stretched upon a rack and dragged, beaten with sinews and clubs. Several days afterward, by Maximian’s order, he was beheaded, together with Largus and Smaragdus and twenty others. This is written in the Acts of Pope Marcellus. At Vienne, Saint Isicius, bishop.

## F. Sixteenth day before the Kalends of April

In Scotland, the commemoration of Saint Patrick, bishop and confessor, who first preached Christ there. On the same day, Saint Gertrude, virgin, and the commemoration of Maria, martyr. She was the servant of a certain distinguished man named Tertullus. Because she refused to attend her master’s banquets on the birthday of his son, preferring instead to devote herself to fasting in the Christian manner, she was cruelly torn by scourging by that same master [Col. 0861B]. But when this could not turn her away from her steadfast service to Christ and bring her back to the worship of idols, she was handed over to the public judge for punishment.

When the executioners wished to consign her to the flames, a reprieve of three days was granted her because of the people’s prayers. When the three days had passed and she was again to be punished, she was miraculously rescued by the Lord’s mercy. For when she had poured out a prayer to the Lord, an enormous rock that had stood before her split open through the middle and received her within itself; closing her in on every side, it resisted the fury. When the people ran together and wished, according to the ruler’s command, to destroy that very stone, lightning and thunder were sent from heaven, and many of them perished, so that 2,700 of them were extinguished by divine judgment. The few who remained, however, were converted to the Lord and continued in the Christian religion.

## G. Fifteenth day before the Kalends of April

The commemoration of Saint Alexander, bishop. Coming from his city in Cappadocia and journeying toward Jerusalem with a longing for the holy places, he arrived when Narcissus, bishop of that city, was already governing the Church in old age. It was revealed to Narcissus and to many of his clergy that on the following morning they should go to meet a bishop who was to be an assistant to the priestly see [Col. 0862B]. Thus, when everything had happened as foretold, and all the people in Palestine had assembled together, Alexander, with Narcissus especially supporting him, assumed with him the governance of the Church of Jerusalem.

When the persecution of Decius came, Alexander was already distinguished by the venerable whiteness of extreme old age. He was taken to Caesarea and shut in prison; for his confession of Christ he was crowned with martyrdom. At Alexandria, the commemoration of Colesticus; at Nicomedia, of Aprilis and Cervolus.

## A. Fourteenth day before the Kalends of April

In the city of Spoleto, the commemoration of blessed John, a man of great holiness and a confessor. He came there as a pilgrim from Sicily, built a monastery in its suburb, and lived there for forty-four years. There he also rested in peace, and there God’s benefits are granted to the present day. On the same day, at Sorrento, Saints Quintus, Quintillus, Quartilla, and Marcus, with nine others. In Lucania, Ingenius, Rogata, and Timothy.

## B. Thirteenth day before the Kalends of April

In Britain, Saint Cuthbert. From being a hermit he became bishop of the Church of Lindisfarne, and from childhood to old age he led a life renowned for signs and miracles. When his body had remained buried for eleven years, it was found incorrupt, as though he had died at that very hour, together with the garment in which it had been covered.

## C. Twelfth day before the Kalends of April

At Monte Cassino, the commemoration of Saint Benedict, abbot, whose life, made glorious by miracles, blessed Pope Gregory records in the books of the *Dialogues* [Col. 0864A]. On the same day, blessed Serapion, hermit. In the territory of Lyons, Saint Lupicinus, abbot, whose life was distinguished by holiness and the glory of miracles.

## D. Eleventh day before the Kalends of April

In Gaul, in the city of Narbonne, Saint Paul, bishop and confessor, a disciple of Christ’s apostles. It is said that he was the same Sergius Paulus, the proconsul, a prudent man, from whom Paul himself took his name because Paul had brought him under the faith of Christ. When the holy Apostle Paul was going to Spain to preach, he left him in the aforementioned city of Narbonne. Having diligently fulfilled the duty of preaching, he was buried renowned for miracles.

In Africa, Saturninus and nine others [Col. 0864B]. At Sebaste, Decronius and Alionius.

## E. Tenth day before the Kalends of April

In Africa, Saints Victorianus, Frumentius, another Frumentius, and two brothers. During the Vandal persecution under Huneric, king of the Arians, they were tortured in Africa with the most savage punishments because of their steadfast Catholic confession and were gloriously crowned. In Africa, the commemoration of Felix and twenty others.

## F. Ninth day before the Kalends of April

At Rome, Saint Pigmenius, priest. He had nourished the apostate and impious Julian from childhood and had also instructed him in sacred letters. But when Julian became emperor and abandoned the practice of piety, he heard that Pigmenius was burying the bodies of the holy martyrs whom Julian was having killed. He sent him this message:

> “Go wherever you wish; for here your life will not be spared. Nevertheless, I repay you for your services—not to you.”

Then Saint Pigmenius [Col. 0865B] went to Persia. After staying there four years, he became blind. Thereafter Pigmenius was warned in a dream to return to Rome. When he returned four months later and was climbing the slope of the Sacred Way begging alms with a boy, he happened to encounter the emperor Julian seated in a golden chariot. Seeing Pigmenius from a distance, Julian ordered him to be summoned and said to him:

> “Glory to my gods and goddesses, because I see you.”

The man of God immediately answered:

> “Glory to my Lord Jesus Christ the Nazarene, crucified, because I do not see you.”

At these words Julian became angry and ordered him to be thrown from the bridge into the Tiber. His body was found and gathered up, and he was buried in the cemetery of Pontianus, not far from Saints Abdon and Sennen. Also the commemoration of Saints Seleucus and Agabus.

## G. Eighth day before the Kalends of April

At Nazareth, a city of Galilee, the Annunciation of the Lord; and at Jerusalem, where our Lord Christ was crucified. At Nicomedia, the commemoration of Dula, the maidservant of a pagan soldier, who was killed for her chastity. At Rome, Quirinus, who was killed by Claudius and thrown into the Tiber, found on the island of Lycaonia, and buried in the cemetery of Pontianus. At Smyrna, the commemoration of Saint Irenaeus, bishop, who, under the prefect Probus during the reign of the emperor Maximian, was first tormented with the most severe tortures, then afflicted for many days in prison, and finally completed his course by beheading.

## A. Seventh day before the Kalends of April

At Rome, on the Lavican Way, in its cemetery, the commemoration of Saint Castulus. He was keeper of the palace wardrobe and a host of the saints. Seized by persecutors, he was hung up three times and examined three times; remaining steadfast in his confession of the Lord, he was thrown into a pit, and a mass of sand was poured over him. Thus he passed to Christ with the palm of martyrdom.

In Libya’s Pentapolis, Theodore, bishop; Irenaeus, deacon; Serapion and Ammonius, readers. At Sirmium, the commemoration of Saint Montanus, priest, who was seized with his wife Maxima and thrown into a river; their bodies were found not far from the city beneath a stone. Also the deposition of Saint Liutger, bishop and confessor.

## B. Sixth day before the Kalends of April

At Jerusalem, the resurrection [Col. 0867B] of our Lord Jesus Christ. In Egypt, blessed John, hermit, a man of admirable holiness, who, filled also with the prophetic spirit, foretold victories over tyrants to the most Christian emperor Theodosius [Col. 0868A].

## C. Fifth day before the Kalends of April

At Caesarea in Palestine, Saints Priscus, Malchus, and Alexander, martyrs. During the persecution of Valerian, they lived on a small estate outside the aforementioned city, where heavenly crowns of martyrdom were being offered. Inflamed by the divine fervor of faith, they went voluntarily to the judge and rebuked him for raging so fiercely against the blood of the pious. He immediately handed them over to the beasts to be devoured in the name of Christ.

At the city of the Cabilonenses, the deposition of King Guntram, who devoted himself so completely to spiritual works that, abandoning the pomp of the world, he distributed his treasures to churches and the poor. At Rome, Pope Sixtus, who occupied the Roman see for eight years. In Africa, the commemoration of Rogatus, Successus, and sixteen others. At Caesarea, Saint Dagalassus.

## D. Fourth day before the Kalends of April

The deposition of Eustasius, abbot and disciple of Saint Columbanus, who was father to nearly six hundred monks. Distinguished by the holiness of his life, he was also renowned for miracles. When Bassus, his accuser, had died by divine will, Eustasius himself handled his body with linen cloths and spices and buried him at Saint Peter’s.

In Africa, Saints Armogastes, Archinimus, and Saturus, confessors. During the Vandal persecution under Genseric, the Arian king, they were shining members of Christ’s Church. They frequently rebuked the wickedness of the Arians with Catholic freedom and, for their confession of the truth, endured many severe punishments and insults; they completed the course of their glorious contest. Also the passion of Saint Achartius.

## E. Third day before the Kalends of April

At Paphos, Tychicus, a disciple of the apostles [Col. 0869B]. In Numidia, at the colony of Cirta, the commemoration of Saints Agapius and Secundinus, bishops and martyrs. During the persecution of Valerian, after a long exile, in the aforementioned city—where at that time the rage of the assailing devil was especially bent, through the blind fury of the pagans and the military offices, on testing the faith of the righteous—they became glorious martyrs from an illustrious priesthood.

With them in the same company suffered Aemilianus, a soldier; Tertulla and Antonia, sacred virgins; and a certain woman with her twin children. Also the commemoration of Domnus, Philipponius, Lacatius, and Niceas, bishops.

## F. The day before the Kalends of April

At Rome, Saint Balbina, virgin, daughter of Quirinus the martyr. This blessed martyr took the collar from the neck of Pope Alexander and, according to his command, went to place it around the neck of his daughter, who suffered from a goiter. Suddenly a boy appeared with a lamp; he was certainly an angel of the Lord. He came to the girl and said:

> “Be saved, remain in virginity, and I shall make you see your bridegroom, who shed his blood for love of you.”

When her father arrived to carry out what had been commanded concerning the collar, he suddenly saw that his daughter was well [Col. 0870B]. She was afterward baptized and instructed by Saint Alexander and remained a virgin, rich in good works. After completing the course of this world, she was buried beside her father, Quirinus the martyr.

In Africa, the commemoration of Anesius; the deposition of Ambrose, bishop; and the commemoration of seven virgins.

# April

It has thirty-one days; the lunar month has twenty-nine.

## G. Kalends of April

At Rome, the most blessed Theodora, sister of the illustrious martyr Hermes, whom blessed Pope Alexander instructed, baptized, and taught the faith of Christ. Under the emperor Aurelian she completed her martyrdom and was buried beside her brother the martyr on the Salarian Way, not far from the city of Rome. On the same day, Saint Venantius, bishop and martyr. In the district of Viunnum, Saint Walaricus, confessor, whose tomb is glorified by frequent miracles.

## A. Fourth day before the Nones of April

The commemoration of Saint Nicetius, bishop of Lyons. His life shone with miracles, and his precious death was likewise commended by miracles. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the passion of Saint Theodosia, virgin. During the time of Diocletian, when she was eighteen years old, she voluntarily joined the holy confessors in prison. She was seized by the prefect Urbanus and tortured on the rack; then weighted with iron and thrust into prison, where by God’s power all her bonds were broken.

After this she was tied to a stone and sunk into the sea; but soon returned unharmed to the shore. She was thrown to the beasts in the amphitheater, but remained untouched by them, and earned martyrdom by beheading. In Africa, Amphianus, Victor, and fourteen others; elsewhere, Marcellus, Saturninus, Satullus, Quiriacus, and Queen Procula.

## B. Third day before the Nones of April

At Thessalonica, the commemoration of the holy virgins Agape and Chionia. Under Diocletian they were first tormented in prison and afterward cast into the fire; but, untouched by the flames after pouring out a prayer to God, they gave up their souls. At Tomis, a city of Scythia, the commemoration of Saints Evagrius and Benignus. At Tauromenium in Sicily, Saint Pancratius.

## C. The day before the Nones of April

At Milan, the deposition of blessed Ambrose, bishop and confessor. Through his zeal, among his other distinctions in teaching and miracles, all Italy was converted to the Catholic faith during the time of the Arian perfidy.

## D. Nones of April

At Thessalonica, the commemoration of Saint Irene, virgin. After enduring imprisonment, she was struck by an arrow by the count Sisinnius, under whom her sisters Agape and Chionia likewise completed their martyrdom. Also in Egypt, the commemoration of Saints Marcianus, Nicanor, and Apollonius. At Caesarea in Lycia, the commemoration of Saint Amphianus.

## E. Eighth day before the Ides of April

At Rome, Saint Sixtus, pope, who governed the Church for ten years, two months, and one day. He suffered during the reign of the emperor Hadrian [Col. 0873B]. At Sirmium, the commemoration of Irenaeus, bishop of that place.

## F. Seventh day before the Ides of April

Hegesippus, a most holy man, who lived near the times of the apostles. From the Lord’s Passion until his own age, he wove together histories of ecclesiastical events and, gathering here and there many things useful to readers, composed five books in which he incorporated the speeches of those whose life he followed. He also reproduced their manner of speaking.

He states that he came to Rome under Anicetus, who was the tenth bishop after blessed Peter, and continued until Eleutherius, bishop of the same city, who had once been Anicetus’s deacon. In his books Hegesippus also relates his former life in pagan philosophy:

> “For I myself,” he says, “had been trained in the Platonic schools. When I heard Christians being defamed and saw them fearless in accepting death and enduring every punishment, I considered that it would be impossible for them to live in wickedness and lust.”

At Rome, Pope Celestine, who governed the Church for eight years. He decreed that the sacred mysteries should be handled only by sacred ministers; and that any bishop who had been summoned to the apostolic see, on returning to his parish, should not be received unless he brought to the people letters of greeting—namely, *formatae*—from the apostolic see.

He also decreed that during the celebration of the Mass the *Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus* should be sung, and that the 150 Psalms of David should be sung antiphonally before the sacrifice. Previously, only the Epistles and the holy Gospel had been read. In Alexandria, the commemoration of Peleusius, priest. At Nicomedia, the commemoration of Cyriacus with ten others.

## G. Sixth day before the Ides of April

At Tours, Saint Perpetuus, bishop, a man of admirable holiness. Through his work, a church was completed over the revered bones of blessed Martin, bishop, and his sacred body was transferred from the place where it had first been buried to the place where it is now duly venerated. In Africa, the commemoration of Januarius, Maxima, and Macarius; and at Carthage, of Concessa.

## A. Fifth day before the Ides of April

At Sirmium, the commemoration of seven virgins who merited being crowned together. At Antioch, blessed Prochorus, deacon, a man renowned for faith and miracles, who completed his course by martyrdom. He was one of the first seven deacons and rests there.

## B. Fourth day before the Ides of April

Ezekiel, prophet. At Rome, many blessed martyrs, whom blessed Pope Alexander and martyr baptized while he was being held in prison, and who were bound together with him. The emperor Aurelian had all of them placed on an old ship, taken out into the open sea, and, with stones fastened around their necks, sunk into the depths [Col. 0876B].

## C. Third day before the Ides of April

At Cortyna, a city of Crete, blessed Philip, bishop, who was renowned for his life and teaching during the reigns of the emperors Antoninus Verus and Lucius Aurelius Commodus.

## D. The day before the Ides of April

At Rome, on the Aurelian Way, at the third milestone, in the cemetery of Calepodius, the commemoration of Saint Julius, bishop and confessor. Under Constantius, the Arian son of Constantine, he endured tribulations and exiles for ten months. After Constantius’s death he returned to his see with great glory.

He decreed that no cleric should conduct any case in public except in a church; that statements of faith should be collected by notaries; and that bonds, instruments, donations, exchanges, transfers, wills, pleadings, and manumissions should be executed by clerics in the church. At Verona, the city, the passion of Saint Zeno, martyr, concerning whom blessed Gregory relates an account in the book of the *Dialogues*.

## E. Ides of April

At Pergamum, a city of Asia, Saints Carp[us], bishop, Papyrus, deacon, and Agathonica, an excellent woman, together with many others, who were crowned with martyrdom through tested confessions. With them was the remarkable man Justin, the philosopher, who even wore the dress of philosophers and labored greatly for the religion of Christ, to the point that he presented Antoninus Pius, his sons, and the senate with a book written against the pagans, and was not ashamed of the disgrace of the cross.

When he had already presented a second book to the successors of the aforementioned emperor, namely Antoninus Verus and Aurelius Commodus, in defense of our religion, he received the reward of a faithful tongue in the gift of martyrdom.

In Spain, the commemoration of Hermenegild, whom his father, King Leovigild, an Arian, seeing his unyielding confession of the Catholic faith, cast into prison and chains. There, on the holy night of the Lord’s Resurrection, by order of his wicked father, he was struck with an axe and entered the heavenly kingdom as king and martyr in place of an earthly kingdom. In the city of Chalcedon, the commemoration of Euphemia, virgin and martyr.

## F. Eighteenth day before the Kalends of May

At Rome, on the Appian Way, in the cemetery of Praetextatus, the commemoration of Saints Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus, martyrs, under the prefect Almachius. The first two were beaten with clubs and struck with the sword; the last was beaten with leaded rods until he gave up his spirit. At Terni, Saint Proculus, martyr. Also Saint Domna, virgin, crowned with her companions, the virgins. At Alexandria, blessed Fronto, abbot, whose life was glorious in holiness and miracles, and who was father to nearly seventy monks.

## G. Seventeenth day before the Kalends of May

In the city of Córdoba, the commemoration of Olympias and Maximus, noble persons. By Decius’s order they were beaten with clubs and then with leaded rods; finally their heads were crushed with axes until they gave up their spirit [Col. 0880A].

In Spain, in the city of Zaragoza, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Optatus, Lupercus, Successus, Martial, Urbanus, Julius, Quintilianus, Publius, Fronto, Felix, Caecilianus, Evotus, Primitivus, Apodemus, and four others, all of whom are reported to have been called Saturninus.

In Italy, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Romanus, Eutyches, and Victorinus, whom Aurelian had killed through various tortures.

## A. Sixteenth day before the Kalends of May

At Corinth, Callistus and Cariphus, with seven others, all drowned in the sea. At Rome, Saint Anicetus, pope, who occupied the episcopal see for eleven years and was crowned with martyrdom during the reigns of Severus and Marcus; he was buried in the cemetery of Callistus. He decreed that the clergy should not grow their hair long, according to the Apostle’s precept.

## B. Fifteenth day before the Kalends of May

In Africa, the commemoration of Saint Mappalicus, who was crowned with martyrdom together with many others. Blessed Cyprian writes much about him in a letter. At Antioch, the commemoration of Saints Peter, deacon, and Hermogenes. At Vienne, Saint Pantagathus, bishop. In Africa, Fortunatus and Marcianus.

## C. Fourteenth day before the Kalends of May

At Messina in Apulia, the commemoration of Eleutherius, bishop and martyr, and Anthia, his mother. Eleutherius was ordained bishop at Aquileia and suffered at Rome under the emperor Hadrian. He first converted Felix and Correbus, his companions, to the faith of Christ; for this, Correbus was struck with the sword.

Eleutherius first overcame an iron bed, then a grating with fire placed beneath it, afterward a frying pan boiling with pitch and fat; then he subdued wild beasts, and finally was slaughtered together with his mother.

At Rome, Saint Apollonius, senator. Under the emperor Commodus he was betrayed by a servant because he was a Christian and was ordered to give an account of his faith. He composed an eminent volume, which he read in the senate, and nevertheless, by the senate’s sentence, was beheaded for Christ [Col. 0882A].

## D. Thirteenth day before the Kalends of May

In Armenia, in the city of Melitene, the commemoration of Saints Hermogenes, Gaius, Expeditius, Aristonichus, Rufus, and Galatha, crowned on one day. In Spain, in the city of Caucoliberis, the commemoration of Saint Vincent, martyr.

At Corinth, blessed Timo[n], one of the first seven deacons. He first sat as a teacher at Beroea; afterward, spreading the word of the Lord, he came to Corinth. There he was handed over by zealous Jews and by Greeks who persecuted the name of Christ. First, as they say, he was thrown into flames but was unharmed; then he was fastened to a cross, completed his martyrdom, and was gloriously buried at Corinth.

## E. Twelfth day before the Kalends of May

At Rome, Saint Victor, bishop, who governed the Church for ten years and was the thirteenth after blessed Peter. He was crowned with martyrdom under the emperor Severus.

He decreed that Holy Easter should be celebrated on Sunday and observed from the fifteenth moon of the first month through the twenty-first. He also decreed that, when necessity required it—whether in a river, at sea, or in springs—people coming from the nations should be baptized under the Christian confession.

In Gaul, in the city of Embrun, the commemoration of Saint Marcellinus, the first bishop and confessor of that city. At Rome, Saints Sulpicius and Servilianus.

## F. Eleventh day before the Kalends of May

At Rome, Saint Soter, pope, who occupied the episcopal see for nine years and was buried in the cemetery of Callistus. He decreed that no nun should touch the consecrated veil in church or place incense.

In Persia, the commemoration of Saint Simeon, bishop of Seleucia and Ctesiphon, royal cities. During the persecution of Sapor, king of the Persians, he was arrested at the tyrant’s command. Loaded with iron and brought before unjust tribunals, he bore witness to the Lord Jesus Christ with a free and most steadfast voice.

First he was confined for a long time in a prison-workhouse with one hundred others, some of whom were bishops, others priests, and others clerics of various orders. Finally he was ordered to be beheaded with them all, so that while the others were being slaughtered he would stand by and be killed last.

With him also suffered Ustazades, a eunuch and the king’s tutor; Abdella and Ananias, venerable old men; and Pusicius, overseer of the royal craftsmen. When he saw the aforementioned old man Ananias trembling beneath the sword, Pusicius cried out boldly:

> “Close your eyes for a little while, old man, without fear; soon you will see the countenance of Christ.”

Pusicius’s daughter, a sacred virgin, was also killed at the same time.

At Alexandria, the commemoration of Fortunatus, Arator the priest, Felix, Silinus, and Vitalis, who rested in prison. In Asia, the commemoration of Maximinus, martyr, who, after other tortures during the time of Decius, was crushed beneath stones.

## G. Tenth day before the Kalends of May

At Rome, on the Appian Way, in the cemetery of Callistus, Pope Gaius. He decreed that anyone who was worthy of becoming a bishop should first ascend through all the grades: doorkeeper, reader, exorcist, subdeacon, deacon, and priest.

After governing the Church for eleven years, four months, and twelve days, he was crowned with martyrdom under the emperor Diocletian, together with his brother Gabinus, a priest.

Agapitus, pontiff, who occupied the Roman see for eleven months. When he entered Constantinople to visit the emperor Justinian, he deposed Anthemius, bishop of Constantinople, who denied the two natures in Christ, and consecrated Mennas, a Catholic, in his place.

In Persia, many holy martyrs who, by order of King Sapor, were arrested throughout the whole region of Persia on the annual day when the memory of the Lord’s Passion is celebrated and slaughtered with the sword for Christ’s name.

In this contest of faith suffered Milesius, bishop, distinguished for holiness and the glory of miracles; Accepsimas, bishop, with his priest James; Mareas and Bicor, bishops, with nearly two hundred clerics and fifty monks; and also many consecrated virgins. Among them were Tarbud, the sister of the holy bishop Simeon, and her maidservant. They tied them to stakes and killed them most cruelly by cutting them apart with saws [Col. 0886A].

In the city of Córdoba, the commemoration of Parmenio, Helimena, and Chrysolitus, priests, and Luke and Mutius, deacons from Babylonia. The first of these continued to speak even after his tongue had been cut out. All were first suspended on the rack and stretched by bonds; then they were burned with hot plates applied to their sides and torn with claws; finally they were slaughtered with the sword in the presence of the persecutor Decius.

At Lyons in Gaul, Saint Epipodius, martyr, under Antoninus Verus. At Vienne, Saint Julian, bishop and confessor.

## A. Ninth day before the Kalends of May

The commemoration of Saint George, martyr [Col. 0886B]. Under Datianus, the most powerful king of the Persians, who ruled over seventy kings, he became renowned for many miracles and converted very many to the faith of Christ. He also strengthened Alexandra, Datianus’s wife, even to martyrdom. Finally, he completed his martyrdom by beheading, although the account of his passion is counted among the apocryphal writings.

In Gaul, in the city of Valence, the commemoration of Saints Felix, priest, Fortunatus and Achilles, deacons [Col. 0887A]. Sent by blessed Irenaeus, bishop and martyr of Lyons, to preach the word of God, they converted the greater part of the aforementioned city to the faith. The commander Cornelius thrust them into prison; afterward they were beaten for a very long time with the harshest scourging of sinews. Then, with their hands bound behind their backs and their legs broken, they were fastened around the turning wheels. Bitter soot was also placed beneath them, and they were suspended day and night by continuous stretching on the rack. Finally they were put to death with the sword.

At the monastery of Fontenelle, Saint Wulfram, bishop, a man distinguished for miracles; and Saint Adalbert, bishop and martyr.

## B. Eighth day before the Kalends of May

At Lyons in Gaul, the commemoration of Saint Alexander. On the third day after blessed Epipodius, he was brought out of prison and first so mangled by the cruelty of his beaters [Col. 0887B] that, when his ribs had been broken apart and his entrails exposed, the secrets of his soul were revealed. Then, fastened to the cross, he gave up his blessed spirit in death.

Thirty-four others suffered with him.

On the same day, the deposition in Britain of Miletus, bishop, who was the third after Augustine to assume the Church of Canterbury. He governed it for five years and was buried in the church of Saint Peter.

On this day Ananias, Azarias, and Misael were delivered from the furnace.

## C. Seventh day before the Kalends of May

At Rome, the greater litany to Saint Peter [Col. 0888A].

At Alexandria, the commemoration of Saint Mark the Evangelist. He was the disciple and interpreter of the Apostle Peter. At the brothers’ request, he wrote the Gospel at Rome. When Peter heard it, he approved it and issued it to the churches for reading on his authority.

After taking it up, Mark went to Egypt. He was the first to announce Christ in Alexandria and established the Church there. After he had established and confirmed churches throughout Libya, Marmarica, Ammonica, the Pentapolis, Alexandria, and all Egypt, he was finally seized by the pagans who remained in Alexandria.

When they saw him celebrating Mass on the holy day of Easter, they threw a rope around his neck and dragged him to the places called Bucolus, which were beside the sea. Beneath the rocks a church had been built; his flesh fell onto the ground and the stones were stained with blood [Col. 0888B].

When evening came, they threw him into prison. There, around midnight, he was first strengthened by an angelic visitation; then the Lord himself appeared to him and called him to the heavenly kingdoms.

In the morning, while he was being dragged to the places of Bucolus, he gave thanks and said:

> “Lord, into your hands I commend my spirit.”

Then he died, and religious men buried him with honor in a place of hewn stone. He had appointed Anianus bishop of Alexandria in his place.

## D. Sixth day before the Kalends of May

At Rome, the commemoration of Saint Anacletus, pope. Having governed the Church for nine years as the fourth after blessed Peter, he was crowned with martyrdom during the persecution of Domitian.

He built a memorial to blessed Peter and arranged places where the bishops might be buried. He was ordained priest by blessed Peter; he was brought to assist at the sacrifice and celebrated it. Later, led to repentance, he was beheaded for confessing the true faith.

He decreed that whenever the holy Gospels were read, priests should not sit but stand bowed.

Also the commemoration of Saint Marcellinus, pope. After governing the Church for nine years and four months, during the reigns of Diocletian and Maximian, he was beheaded by Diocletian himself for the faith of Christ, together with Claudius, Quirinus, and Antoninus. Thirty-five days later he was buried on the Salarian Way, in a chamber, by the priest Marcellus and the deacons, with hymns.

At that time there was a great persecution, so that within one month 18,000 people of both sexes were crowned with martyrdom in various provinces. At Vienne, Saint Clarentius, bishop and confessor.

## E. Fifth day before the Kalends of May

At Rome, Saint Anastasius, pope [Col. 0891A], who sat after blessed Peter as the forty-first bishop for three years and ten days. Finding Manichaeans in the city of Rome, he condemned them and established that no foreigner should be received into the clergy unless he presented a document written by five bishops.

At Nicomedia, the commemoration of Saint Anthimus, bishop and martyr. During the persecution of Diocletian, he earned the glory of martyrdom by beheading for his confession of Christ. Almost the whole multitude of his flock followed him as a good shepherd. The aforementioned tyrant ordered some of them to be beheaded with the sword, others to be burned in the fire, and others to be placed in small boats and sunk in the sea. This is written in the *Ecclesiastical History*.

## F. Fourth day before the Kalends of May

At Ravenna, the commemoration of Saint Vitalis, martyr, who was the father of Saints Gervasius and Protasius.

He was a soldier and a consular official, and entered Ravenna with his judge Paulinus. When he saw before his judge a Christian named Ursicinus, a physician by profession and a Ligurian by birth, receive a capital sentence after many tortures, and when he saw him already approaching the palm and becoming afraid, Vitalis cried out:

> “Do not, Ursicinus the physician—you who were accustomed to heal others—wound yourself with the dart of eternal death; and you who have come through great sufferings to the palm, do not lose the crown prepared for you by the Lord.”

Hearing this, Ursicinus knelt and urged the executioner to strike him, repenting that he had been afraid.

When Ursicinus had completed his martyrdom, Vitalis buried him within the city of Ravenna and himself refused to appear any longer before the judge. He was therefore seized by the consular official Paulinus, chiefly because he had strengthened Ursicinus by his exhortations. After the tortures of the rack, he was ordered to be taken to the Palm—a place where Christians were beheaded, so called because palm trees grew there.

A pit was dug until water was found. Vitalis was placed there on his back and buried beneath earth and stones.

At Alexandria, Saint Theodora, virgin, of whom blessed Ambrose writes: although she refused to sacrifice and was handed over to a brothel, she was rescued by God’s wondrous favor. When a crowd of shameless young men was already standing at the door of her cell, suddenly one of the brothers, named Didymus, full of faith and divinely inspired, burst into the brothel first. Explaining to the holy virgin why he had come, he put military clothing on her and himself put on virginal garments.

Thus the virgin left and escaped toward the city, recognized by no one. Didymus was brought before the governor. He firmly explained everything, confessed that he was a Christian, and was beheaded and given to the fire. The blessed virgin, who had fled from the brothel to protect her integrity, returned to the arena out of love for the crown. She was struck down together with Didymus and crowned together with him.

In Pannonia, Saint Pollio, martyr [Col. 0894A], and Saints Aphrodisius, Caralippus, Agapius, and Eusebius, martyrs.

### G. Third day before the Kalends of May

At the city of Santones, the feast of Saint Eutropius the martyr, who was sent into Gaul by Blessed Clement, bishop, and was also consecrated by him with the dignity of the episcopal order. Having fulfilled the duties of this office and completed his preaching among unbelievers, when the pagans rose against him, he victoriously fell after his head had been struck.

Finally, after many years had passed, when Palladius, bishop of that same city, together with other men of God, was transferring his body into a new basilica for the sake of the honor due to him, they opened the sarcophagus and saw on his head the scar at the place where the edge of the axe had been fixed. When the priests had retired to rest on the following night, he appeared to them in a vision and said: “Know that I completed my martyrdom through the scar which you saw on my head.” [Col. 0894B]

Also, the feast of Saints Marianus and James, the former of whom was a lector and the latter a deacon.

At Rome, Saint Cletus, pope, who was the third bishop of the city of Rome after Peter. He held the episcopate for twelve years and was crowned with martyrdom there under the emperor Domitian; and Saint Maximus the martyr.

### A. The day before the Kalends of May

At Rome, Saint Quirinus, tribune and martyr, under the emperor Trajan. When, at Trajan’s command, he had imprisoned Blessed Alexander, pope, and Hermes, the prefect, he had a daughter whose neck was surrounded by a swelling. After hearing Blessed Hermes’s exhortations concerning faith in Christ and seeing the signs that the Lord performed through his martyrs Alexander and Hermes, he offered this same daughter to them for healing. Blessed Alexander said to her:

“Take the collar from my neck and place it on her.”

When the father obediently carried this out, she was suddenly healed by divine will. Her name was Balbina, and thus her father, together with all those who were being held in custody, and his entire household, was baptized.

When the clerk Aurelianus reported this to the judge, Aurelianus became angry, ordered Quirinus to be brought before him, and said to him: “I loved you as a son, but you mocked me, deceived by Alexander.” [Col. 0895A]

Quirinus said to him: “I have become a Christian. If you wish to kill me, kill me; if you wish to beat me, beat me; if you wish to burn me, burn me. I will be nothing else. For I caused all who were in the prison to become Christians, and I released them, but they refused to go anywhere.”

Aurelianus, enraged, had his tongue cut out and then had him suspended on the torture-horse. Since he did not yield to Aurelianus’s violence, Aurelianus ordered his hands and feet to be cut off, then ordered him to be beheaded and thrown to the dogs. But Christians seized his body on the Appian Way and buried it in the cemetery of Praetextatus.

At Alexandria, the feast of Ephrodisius the presbyter and thirty others; and the vigil of the apostles Philip and James.

### May

The month has thirty-one days; the moon, thirty.

### B. The Kalends of May

The prophet Jeremiah.

And the feast of the holy apostles Philip and James, sons of Mary, who was the sister of the Lord’s Mother. Of these, Philip, after having nearly converted Scythia to the faith of Christ and having established deacons, presbyters, and bishops there, returned to Asia and fell asleep in peace at Hierapolis.

James, who is also read of as the Lord’s brother, was immediately after the Lord’s Passion ordained bishop of Jerusalem by the apostles. He was holy from his mother’s womb: he drank neither wine nor strong drink, ate no meat, was never shorn, was never anointed with ointment, and never used a bath. To him alone it was permitted to enter the Holy of Holies. Indeed, he did not wear woolen garments but linen ones; he alone entered the temple and prayed for the people on bended knees, to such an extent that his knees appeared to have acquired the hardness of camels. [Col. 0897A]
