First he was grievously tortured and beaten; then, bound with chains and stretched upon a grate, he was drenched with vinegar and mustard [Col. 0986A]. When he appeared unharmed by the fire, he was again bound with iron and thrust back into custody. There he was comforted by divine radiance; then he was beaten with the utmost cruelty with iron and ox-hide cords. Finally, sentence was pronounced: “We order that Cucuphas the rebel be struck with the sword.” His body was buried by Christians.

D. SEVENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF AUGUST. The commemoration of blessed Erastus, who, left by blessed Paul as bishop at Philippi, was crowned there with martyrdom and came to rest. At Rome, in the port, Saint Hyacinthus, under the consul Leontius, when Luxurius, the first citizen of Terracina, handed him over [Col. 0987A]. Cast into the fire, he could in no way be harmed. Then thrown into a very powerful torrent, he was cast out unharmed upon the shore. These things were reported to the consul Leontius, who sent a swordsman with soldiers to seize him and strike him with the sword. Julia gathered his body by night with her servants and buried it honorably on her estate near the city of Rome. In Phrygia, Saints Jovianus and Julianus.

E. SIXTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF AUGUST. At Nicomedia [Col. 0988A], the commemoration of Saint Hermolaus the presbyter, whose teaching converted blessed Pantaleon to the faith. When he was seized by Maximian together with his two kinsmen Hermippus and Hermocrates, he was punished by capital sentence for confessing Christ. In Sicily, Simeon the monk. In the city of Nola, Felix, Julia, and Jucunda. At Auxerre, the commemoration of Saint Aetherius, bishop.

F. FIFTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF AUGUST. At Nicomedia, the passion of Saint Pantaleon the martyr, who, while learning the art of medicine at the command of Maximian [Col. 0989A], was converted to the faith of Christ by the presbyter Hermolaus. He performed many miracles and brought his father, the senator Eustorgius, under the faith of Christ. For this reason he was seized by that same Maximian and tortured with the punishment of the rack and the burning of lamps [Col. 0990A]. But when the Lord appeared to him amid these torments, he was refreshed. Finally, he completed his martyrdom by a sword-stroke. At Lyons, Saint Peregrinus the presbyter.

G. FOURTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF AUGUST. At Rome, Saint Felix the pontiff. He declared Constantius, the son of Constantine, to be a heretic when he was rebaptized a second time by Eusebius, bishop of Nicomedia; at the command of that same emperor Constantius Augustus, he was beheaded [Col. 0991A]. He sat in the episcopate for one year, three months, and two days. On the same day, the passion of Saints Simplicius and Faustinus, brothers, who at Rome under Diocletian and Maximian, on account of the faith of Christ, were beheaded after many different punishments. Their sister, named Beatrice, because she buried their bodies with the presbyters Crispus and John, was strangled by the prefect Lucretius and gave up her spirit. Lucretius, seized by an unclean spirit, died at his own banquet. Also the burial of blessed Lupus, bishop, who came to Britain with Germanus and exercised the priesthood for fifty-two years. In the time of King Attila, who was ravaging Gaul, as it is sung in his hymn, while all the battles were being lost, he fortified Troyes by prayer. Also the burial of blessed Prosper, bishop.

A. THIRD DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF AUGUST. At Rome, Abdon and Sennen, subordinate kings of the Persians. When they were suffering imprisonment at Corduba, a city of Persia, under Decius, he finally brought them to Rome in chains, where they were tormented with various punishments; first they were beaten with leaded clubs, then killed with the sword. In Africa, in the city of Taburba, the torch-bearing passion of the holy virgins Maxima, Donatilla, and Secunda under Anullinus the proconsul. After enduring many sufferings for Christ, they were struck with the sword and completed their martyrdom. At Auxerre, the burial of Saint Ursus, bishop.

B. DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF AUGUST. At Caesarea, the passion of Saint Fabius [Col. 0993A]. When he refused to carry the standards of the governor, he was first thrust into prison; afterward brought out and interrogated, he persevered in his confession of Christ. Soon the furious judge condemned him to death. After this, his body was sewn into a net, and the head separately from the corpse [Col. 0994A] was sunk into the depths of the sea. But by the Lord’s power, the body was restored intact, carried to the shore of Carenium, and buried with fitting honor by the faithful in a basilica. In Africa, the commemoration of Saints Democritus, Secundus, Dionysius, and Thyrsus. At Ravenna, the translation of Saint Germanus, bishop and confessor.

AUGUST. It has thirty-one days; the moon, twenty-nine.

[Col. 0993B]

C. KALENDS OF AUGUST. The seven holy Maccabean brothers with their mother, who suffered under King Antiochus. At Rome, the dedication of the first church built and consecrated by blessed Peter. At Vienne, Saint Verus, bishop, who was one of the disciples of the apostles, and Saint Nectarius, bishop. At Vercelli, Eusebius [Col. 0994B], bishop, who, when the Arians stirred up persecution under the emperor Constantius, suffered martyrdom. In the city of Philadelphia, the commemoration of the holy martyrs Cyril, Aquila, Peter, Domitian, Rufus, and Menander, crowned on one day. In the city of Gerunda, the commemoration of Saint Felix the martyr, whom Rufinus ordered to be torn apart for so long that he finally died.

[Col. 0995A]

D. FOURTH DAY BEFORE THE NONES OF AUGUST. At Rome, Saint Stephen, pope and martyr, under the emperors Valerian and Gallienus. When savage persecution was raging, he gathered all his clergy and urged them to receive the crown of martyrdom gladly for Christ. He established that priests and deacons should not use sacred vestments in daily life, but only in church. He had ordained three priests, seven deacons, and ten clerics, with whom he continually taught about the kingdom of God. Blessed Stephen, after performing many good works, was ordered to be beheaded when soldiers sent by Valerian arrived. They found him offering sacrifice to God and beheaded him in that same place. Christians buried his body in the same crypt where his blood had been shed, in the place called the cemetery of Callistus [Col. 0996A]. He sat in the episcopate for seven years, five months, and three days. On the same day, the commemoration of Saint Theodota, with her three sons, in the province of Bithynia, in the city of Nicaea, in the time of Diocletian, under the count Leucadius. He bound her with iron together with her sons and sent them to Nicetius, the governor of Bithynia. The latter had her firstborn son Evodius, who boldly confessed Christ, beaten with clubs, and then burned her with all her sons. This is written in the Passion of Saint Anastasia.

E. THIRD DAY BEFORE THE NONES OF AUGUST. At Jerusalem, the discovery of the body of Saint Stephen the protomartyr and of Saints Gamaliel, Nicodemus, and Abibon, as it was revealed by the Lord to blessed Lucian the presbyter in the seventh year of the emperor Honorius. Also at Antioch, Saint Stephen [Col. 0997A] the protomartyr, where one of the stones with which he was struck in the arm is said to be kept, and through it many works of healing are performed. At Constantinople, the commemoration of Saint Hermellus the martyr.

F. DAY BEFORE THE NONES OF AUGUST. The commemoration of blessed Aristarchus, concerning whom blessed Paul the apostle writes to the Colossians: “Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you.” He remained the Apostle’s constant companion until his confession; appointed bishop of the Thessalonians, he came to rest, crowned by Christ, after long and most blessed struggles. At Rome, in the sand-pit crypt, blessed Tertullian the martyr, whom blessed Stephen baptized and ordained presbyter while he was clothed in white. Not long afterward he earned martyrdom by the cutting off of his head and was buried by blessed Stephen the pontiff [Col. 0998A]. Also the commemoration of Saint Justin the confessor. At Lyons, the arrival of the body of Saint Justus, bishop, from the wilderness.

G. THE NONES OF AUGUST. At Autun, Saint Cassian, bishop. In the city of Châlons, the burial of Memmius, bishop and confessor; and elsewhere, Saints Florian and Philistina. Also the commemoration of Saint Oswald, king, crowned with martyrdom.

[Col. 0999A]

A. EIGHTH DAY BEFORE THE IDES OF AUGUST. At Rome, in the cemetery of Callistus on the Appian Way, the commemoration of Saint Sixtus, bishop and martyr, under the emperor Decius and the prefect Valerian, and of Saints Felicissimus and Agapitus, his deacons, whom Decius ordered to be beheaded together before the temple of Mars. At night the clergy and a great number of Christians came and buried the bodies of the saints with due honor. Four other men were beheaded with them, as is read in the Acts of the Pontiffs: Januarius, Magnus, Vincentius, and Stephen, subdeacons. Blessed Quartus also suffered with them, as Saint Cyprian writes. This blessed Sixtus was born and educated at Athens; first a philosopher, he later became a disciple of Christ. He sat in the episcopate for one year, ten months, and twenty-three days. In Spain, in the city of Complutum, the commemoration of the brothers Justus and [Col. 0999B] Pastor. While they were still boys being instructed in letters, they threw down their writing tablets in school and ran of their own accord to martyrdom [Col. 1000A]. Soon, at the command of Dacianus, they were slaughtered by executioners; they also rest there in the basilica bearing their name. Also the commemoration of Pope Hormisdas, who sat at Rome for seventeen years. He organized the clergy and taught the psalms. During his time, the heretical emperor Anastasius was struck by lightning and died. The same pontiff was buried in the church of blessed Peter.

B. SEVENTH DAY BEFORE THE IDES OF AUGUST. In Tuscany, in the city of Arezzo, the commemoration of Saint Donatus, bishop and martyr. He was seized in the time of the emperor Julian by Quadratianus, the Augustal prefect, together with Hilarinus the monk, and ordered to sacrifice to idols. When he refused, he ordered Hilarinus to be beaten with clubs in his presence until he gave up his spirit; afterward he ordered blessed Donatus to be struck with the sword [Col. 1000B]. Christians buried their bodies reverently near the city [Col. 1001A]. Blessed Gregory mentions him, saying that through prayer he restored a shattered chalice. At Rome, the holy martyrs Peter and Juliana, with eighteen others. At Milan, Saint Faustinus, martyred in the time of Aurelius Commodus. In the province of Raetia, in the city of Augusta, the commemoration of Saint Afra the martyr.

C. SIXTH DAY BEFORE THE IDES OF AUGUST. At Rome, on the Ostian Way, at the seventh milestone, the commemoration of Saint Cyriacus the martyr. Blessed Marcellus, together with Lucina, a most Christian matron, transferred him and the bodies of the other saints who suffered with him to her estate, embalming them with spices and placing them in linen wrappings in stone sarcophagi, on the eighth day of August. The passions of the blessed martyrs—namely Cyriacus, Largus, and Smaragdus—are recorded in various places [Col. 1002A]; that is, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April. At Vienne, the commemoration of Saint Severus, presbyter and confessor, who also converted a great multitude of pagans to the faith of Christ by his word and miracles.

D. FIFTH DAY BEFORE THE IDES OF AUGUST. At Rome, Saint Romanus the soldier, who, moved by the confession of Saint Laurence, asked to be baptized by him. Soon, at the command of Decius, he was brought forward with clubs and beheaded. In the city of Verona, the passion of Saints Firmus and Rusticus, who suffered in the time of the emperor Maximian and the consul Anolinus. Also the vigil of Saint Laurence.

E. FOURTH DAY BEFORE THE IDES OF AUGUST. The commemoration of Saint Laurence, archdeacon [Col. 1003A], under Decius. After many tortures—imprisonment, scourging, and various plates of heated metal—he finally completed his martyrdom by being roasted on an iron grate. At the first light of morning, Hippolytus took away his body and, together with the presbyter Justin, embalmed it with linen and spices in the evening; they buried it in the Veranian field. At Rome, sixty-five soldiers. At that time Claudius, Severus, Crescentius, and Romanus also suffered on the same day.

F. THIRD DAY BEFORE THE IDES OF AUGUST. At Rome, between the two laurel trees, the commemoration of Saint Tiberius the martyr, who, at the command of the governor Fabianus, walked barefoot over burning coals and was not harmed at all. Later, through the plotting of the apostate Torquatus, the aforementioned Fabianus pierced him with a sword, and he completed his martyrdom. Also at Rome, the commemoration of Saint Susanna, virgin, who was the daughter of Gabinius the presbyter [Col. 1003B], brother of Pope Gaius. Under the emperor Diocletian she suffered because she refused to be joined in marriage to his son Maximus, wishing to remain a virgin. Pope Gaius and Serena Augusta encouraged her to remain steadfast in faith and perpetual chastity. For this reason, after other tortures, Diocletian ordered her to be struck with a sword in her own house [Col. 1004A], and thus she completed her martyrdom. The aforementioned Serena Augusta gathered the body of the holy virgin and wiped away with her own veil the blood she had shed in that same place; she placed it in a silver chest in her palace, where she did not cease to pray day and night at secret intervals. She herself adorned the body of Saint Susanna with linen wrappings and spices and placed it beside the bodies of the saints in the cemetery of Alexander. Also the burial of Gaugericus, bishop and confessor, who governed the Church of Cambrai for thirty-three years.

G. DAY BEFORE THE IDES OF AUGUST. In Sicily, in the city of Catania, the commemoration of Euplius the deacon. After being tortured for a very long time, he was beheaded by the consul Calvisianus in the time of Diocletian and Maximian. On the same day, Saint Hilaria, mother of Saint Afra the martyr. While she kept vigil at her daughter’s tomb [Col. 1004B], she was handed over to the fire there by persecutors for the faith of Christ, together with Digna and Eumenia and Euprepia, who had been Saint Afra’s maidens. In Syria, the commemoration of Saints Macarius and Julian.

A. THE IDES OF AUGUST. At Rome, Saint Hippolytus, who in the time of Decius, with his feet bound to the necks of untamed horses, was dragged through thistles and thorns [Col. 1005A] and so gave up his spirit. Also the commemoration of Concordia, his nurse, whom he martyred before himself by having her beaten with leaded clubs, and of nineteen others from his household, who were beheaded together. On the same day, the commemoration at Rome of Saint Cassianus. When he refused to worship idols, the persecutor asked him what trade he practiced. He replied that he taught children their letters. Immediately stripped of his clothing and bound with his hands behind his back, he was placed in the midst of them. The children whom he had made hateful to himself by teaching were summoned and given permission to kill him. Just as much as they had grieved while learning, so much did they rejoice in taking revenge. Some beat him with tablets and boxes of boxwood; others wounded him with their writing-styles. The weaker their hands were, the more grievous a punishment they inflicted by prolonging his death. At Poitiers, the burial of Saint Radegund, queen. In the province of Germany, the commemoration of Saint Wigbert, presbyter and confessor.

B. NINETEENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. The commemoration of Saint Eusebius, presbyter and confessor, who under the Arian emperor Constantius, through the machination of Liberius the bishop, likewise a heretic, completed his confession. For the aforementioned Constantius shut him up in a certain small room of his house, four feet wide. There he persevered in prayer for many days and, on the tenth day before the Kalends of September, after seven months, while still confined, received his falling-asleep. The presbyters Gregory and Orosius gathered his body and buried it in a crypt beside the body of blessed Sixtus, bishop and martyr, on the Appian Way, in the cemetery of Callistus. There, writing his epitaph, they placed it as follows: “To Eusebius, a man of God.” When Constantius heard that Gregory and Orosius had buried the body of blessed Eusebius, he ordered Gregory to be shut alive into the same crypt where they had placed it. Orosius removed him from there by night, half alive, and shortly afterward buried him, when dead, beside the body of Saint Eusebius. A very severe persecution then arose against the catholic Church [Col. 1006B], while Liberius occupied the apostolic see. Also the vigil of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary.

C. EIGHTEENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. The Assumption of holy Mary, Mother of God and perpetual virgin. On the same day [Col. 1007A], Saint Tarsicius, acolyte and martyr. When pagans found him carrying the sacrament of Christ’s body, they began to question him about what he was carrying. Judging it unworthy to cast pearls before swine, he was beaten with clubs and stones until he breathed out his spirit. When the sacrilegious questioners searched his overturned body, they were unable to find any of Christ’s sacraments. Christians gathered the martyr’s body and buried it in the cemetery of Callistus. At Nicomedia, Saints Strato, Philip, and Eutychianus, with their companions.

D. SEVENTEENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. At Nicaea in Bithynia, the commemoration of Saint Ursatius the confessor, under Licinius the persecutor. Abandoning military service, he chose a solitary life in a certain tower of the aforementioned city. He shone with such great virtues [Col. 1007B] that he is said both to have driven out demons and, by praying, to have killed an enormous dragon [Col. 1008A]. At Rome, Saint Serena, formerly the wife of Diocletian Augustus. In Alexandria, Saints Orion, Aemilius, and Ignatius. In Persia, Saint Thyrsus with his companions. At Metz, Saint Arnulf the confessor.

E. SIXTEENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. In Africa, the holy martyrs Liberatus the abbot, Boniface the deacon, Servus and Rusticus the subdeacons, Rogatus and Septimus the monks, and Maximus the boy. During the Vandal persecution, at the command of the most savage king Huneric, they were dragged from the monastery dwelling in the territory of the city of Capsa and brought to Carthage. There, for confessing the faith, they were handed over to prison custody and fastened with cruel iron weights. Finally, the tyrant ordered a ship to be filled with bundles of wood and, after they had all been bound together in it, fire to be set beneath them in the middle of the sea [Col. 1008B]. By God’s will the fire was extinguished [Col. 1009A]. Then he ordered them to be killed one by one with the handles of oars, their brains crushed like those of dogs. Their bodies were thrown into the sea, but at that same hour they were returned to the shores and buried by the Christian people in the monastery of Celerina. At Caesarea in Cappadocia, the commemoration of Saint Mammes the martyr, who suffered under the emperor Aurelian and the governor Alexander. On the same day, the octave of Saint Laurence the martyr and confessor.

F. FIFTEENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. At Praeneste, the commemoration of Saint Agapitus the martyr, who under King Antiochus suffered for Christ when he was a boy of fifteen [Col. 1010A]. He was beaten with cords and most atrocious scourges, then hung naked with his head turned downward. A thick black smoke was made beneath him, and boiling water was poured over his belly. Afterward he was thrown to lions, but was not harmed by them; finally he was beheaded. His body was taken away by Christians at night and placed in a new sarcophagus, which had been found there by divine providence. At Rome, the blessed presbyters John and Crispus, who during the persecution buried many bodies of saints with the greatest devotion and afterward came to rest in peace.

G. FOURTEENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. The commemoration of Saint Magnus. In [Col. 1011A] Gaul, Saint Donatus the presbyter, who led an anchoritic life for many years. At Rome, blessed Julius, senator and martyr. Blessed martyrs Eusebius, Vincentius, Peregrinus, and Pontianus instructed him. Through their hands he distributed his possessions to the poor and received baptism from blessed Rufinus the presbyter. When the emperor Commodus heard this, he became angry and handed him over to the judge Vitellius to investigate his possessions and compel him to sacrifice. The judge threw him into prison, then after three days had him brought before him bound in chains. After hearing him, he ordered him to be beaten with clubs until he gave up his spirit. The aforementioned holy martyrs gathered his body by night and buried him in the cemetery of Calepodius.

A. THIRTEENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. Samuel the prophet, whose sacred bones Augustus Arcadius transferred from Judaea to Thrace. Bishops carried them, and the people of all the churches ran to meet them with such joy as though they were receiving him alive [Col. 1011B–1012A]. On the same day, blessed Porphyrius, who instructed the holy martyr Agapitus in the faith and teaching of Christ. In Alexandria, the commemoration of Dioscorus; elsewhere, of Philibert the abbot. In Luciana, Saints Valentinus and Leontius. In the city of Sinnada, Saints Valens, Piricius, Arcius, Maximus, Pamphilus, and Colobus the confessor, and Saint Bernard the abbot.

B. TWELFTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. In the territory of the city of Gamala, the commemoration of Saint Privatus, martyr and bishop, who suffered in the persecution of Valerian and Gallienus. On the same day, the commemoration of Saints Bonosus and Maximianus, whose acts are preserved. In the city of Salona, the commemoration of Anastasius the martyr. When he saw blessed Agapitus boldly confessing Christ amid torments, he cried out [Col. 1012B]: “Great is the God of the Christians, and there is none besides him.” He was a military cornicularius [a soldier holding the rank of cornicularius]. [Col. 1013A] The governor said to him: “As I see, you have been led astray.” The governor reported this to the emperor Aurelian, who immediately ordered him to be killed. Thus he became a martyr and departed to the Lord. In Spain, Vincentius and Julianus. In Sardinia, Saints Luxurius and Trajanus.

C. ELEVENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. The commemoration of Saint Timothy, who came from Antioch to Rome and was received as a guest by Pope Melchiades at the house of Pope Sylvester, who afterward became bishop. After preaching for a whole year and several months and converting many to Christ, he was seized by Tarquinius, prefect of the city, and tormented by a long imprisonment. When he refused to sacrifice to idols, he was beaten three times and subjected to the most severe punishments; finally he was beheaded and buried beside blessed Paul the apostle. At Autun, Saint Symphorianus [Col. 1013B]. In the time of the emperor Aurelian, under the consul Heraclius, when he refused to sacrifice to idols, he was first afflicted with scourging, then committed to prison, and finally, after his head was cut off, completed his martyrdom. In the Roman port, the holy pilgrim martyrs Martial, Epictetus, Saturninus, Aprilis, and Felix [Col. 1014A], with their companions. Also at Rome, blessed Antoninus the martyr. When he was an executioner, he saw a young man standing with a sponge and wiping the sides of the holy martyrs Eusebius, Pontianus, Peregrinus, and Vincentius while they were hanging on the rack and being beaten. He began to exclaim: “Truly Christ is God, whom these men proclaim.” He secretly fled and was baptized by the presbyter Rufinus. Returning to Vitellius and openly confessing himself a Christian, he was condemned to death and buried on the Aurelian Way. On the same day, the octave of the Assumption of Saint Mary.

D. TENTH DAY BEFORE THE KALENDS OF SEPTEMBER. The commemoration of the holy martyrs Donatus, Restitutus, Valerianus, Fructuosa, and twelve others, crowned at Antioch. On the same day, blessed Zacchaeus, bishop, who was the fourth after James to govern the Church of Jerusalem [Col. 1014B]. At Lyons, the holy martyrs Minervus and Eleazar with eight sons. At the port of the city of Rome, Saints Hippolytus, Quiriacus, and Archilaus. At Reims, Saints Timothy and Apollinaris, who were martyred there. In Alexandria, blessed Theonas, the venerable one. The passion of three brothers in the city of Aegeae under the governor Lysias: namely Claudius, Asterius, and Neon. Also the vigil of Saint Bartholomew the apostle.

### E. Ninth day before the Kalends of September

The feast of Saint Bartholomew the apostle, who, while preaching the Gospel of Christ in India, was flayed alive by barbarians and, by order of King Astragis, completed his martyrdom by decapitation. His most sacred body was first transferred to the island of Lipara, which lies near Sicily, and then to Benevento, where it is honored with the devout veneration of the faithful.

At Carthage, the saints who suffered in the time of Valerian and Gallienus. For, among other punishments, they say that the governor then had a lime kiln fired, and burning coals with incense were displayed before its mouth. The governor said to the Christians: “Choose one of these two alternatives: either offer incense to Jupiter upon these coals, or you will be thrown into the lime.”

Then three hundred men, armed with faith, confessed in a swift utterance that Christ, the Son of God, is God, and threw themselves into the fire. Amid the vapors of the lime they were reduced to powder. Hence that army of the blessed deserved also to be called the “White Mass” (*Massa Candida*).

[Col. 1016A]

[Col. 1017A]

### F. Eighth day before the Kalends of September

The Passion of Genesius the martyr under the emperor Diocletian. He had first been a mime or master of the theatrical art while still a pagan [the text reads *minus*, apparently an OCR-corrupted form], but afterward became a confessor of Christ. He was tortured in many ways by the persecutors: beaten with clubs, suspended on the rack, burned with flames, and finally beheaded.

At Rome, the feast of the four holy martyrs Eusebius, Pontianus, Peregrinus, and Vincentius, under the emperor Commodus and the judge Vitellius. First they were raised upon the rack, stretched with cords, and beaten with clubs; flames were applied to their sides, but they were not overcome. Eusebius spoke even after his tongue had been cut out. Finally they were slaughtered with leaded scourges until their spirit departed.

[Col. 1018A]

The blessed presbyter Rufinus gathered their bodies and buried them.

[Col. 1019A]

Also, Saint Genesius of Arles, who was beheaded on the bank of the Rhône River and, baptized in his own blood, received the glory of martyrdom.

On the same day, Saint Sandradas the abbot.

### G. Seventh day before the Kalends of September

At Rome, Saint Zephyrinus the pope, who ruled the Church for eight years, seven months, and ten days. He decreed that, in the presence of all the clergy and faithful laity, whether a deacon or a priest was being ordained, priests should stand by and celebrate Masses.

Also, the feast at Rome of Saints Irenaeus and Abundius, whom Valerian ordered to be thrown into a sewer during the persecution of Decius, because they had lifted out the body of Saint Concordia after it had been cast into the sewer.

[Col. 1020A]

The presbyter Justin also lifted their bodies and buried them in a crypt beside Saint Lawrence.

At Victimilium, a fortress of Italy, Saint Secundus the martyr, from the Theban Legion.

At Pergamum, Saint Alexander the martyr, who likewise belonged to the aforementioned legion of saints and completed his martyrdom by decapitation.

### A. Sixth day before the Kalends of September

At Capua, the feast of Saint Rufus the martyr, whom the blessed Apollinaris, a disciple of the apostle Peter, taught and baptized, when Rufus was of patrician rank.

At Tomis, the holy martyrs Marcellinus the tribune, his wife Mannea, their son John, Serapion the cleric, and Peter the soldier.

[Col. 1021A]

In Gaul, at the city of Arles, Saint Caesarius the bishop and confessor, a man of extraordinary holiness.

At Autun, Saint Siagrius the bishop and confessor.

[Col. 1022A]

### B. Fifth day before the Kalends of September

The feast of the blessed Hermes the martyr. When the blessed Alexander was prefect of the city of Rome, he baptized Hermes together with his wife, his children, and his sister Theodora.

[Col. 1023A]

He baptized with him also 1,250 of his slaves, together with their wives and children, after first granting them their freedom. Not long afterward Hermes was executed by the sword by Aurelian. The blessed Theodora gathered his body and buried it on the Salarian Way.

In Africa, the deposition of Saint Augustine the bishop, who was first transferred from his own city to Sardinia because of the barbarians, and recently brought back to Pavia by King Liutprand of the Lombards and honorably buried there.

[Col. 1024A]

At Constantinople, Saint Alexander the bishop and confessor. Through the power of his prayer, Arius was condemned by divine judgment and burst apart at the middle, and his entrails poured out.

[Col. 1025A]

At Saintes, Saint Julian the bishop and confessor.

Also, the feast of Saint Julian the martyr.

Also, the feast of Saint Pelagius the martyr.

### C. Fourth day before the Kalends of September

The Passion and decapitation—or rather, the discovery of the head—of the blessed John the Baptist, whom Herod, as the Evangelists report, ordered to be beheaded.

At Rome, on the Aventine, in the district of Vindmense, at the Arch of Faustinus, Saint Sabina the martyr, who had once been the wife of the most distinguished Valentinus. The blessed virgin Serapia instructed her in the true faith.

The handmaid of Christ, Sabina, suffered under the emperor Hadrian and the prefect Elpidius. Remaining steadfast in her confession of Christ, she gained the palm of martyrdom by the decapitation of her head. Her body was buried in the tomb that she herself had prepared, where she had previously buried her teacher Serapia.

[Col. 1025B]

At Venusia, a city of Apulia, the feast of Felix the bishop.

At the city of Tubzoz, Januarius the presbyter, and Fortunatianus and Septimus the readers, who under the emperor Diocletian were brought to completion by the sword at the hands of the procurator Magdellianus.

### D. Third day before the Kalends of September

At Rome, on the Ostian Way, Saint Felix the presbyter, under the emperors Diocletian and Maximian, with Draco as prefect and judge.

When he had been brought to the judge’s tribunal beside the temple of Serapis and was being forced to sacrifice, [Col. 1026A] he blew upon the face of the bronze statue, and it immediately fell. Then he was led to the statue of Mercury, which likewise fell. Then he was led to the image of Diana, which fell in the same way.

The governor then ordered him to be beheaded. A certain Christian man met him—hidden from human beings but manifest to God—and began to cry out: “I worship the very one whom this holy Father confesses, the Lord Jesus Christ.”

At once he too was seized by the prefect’s officials. After first exchanging with the blessed Felix the kiss of peace, he was beheaded together with him. Since the Christians afterward could not discover his name, they called him Adauctus, because he had been added to the holy martyr Felix for the crown.

[Col. 1026B]

The Christians came by night and buried them there in the same place. The pagans afterward wished to dig up their bodies, but whoever laid hands upon them was seized by the devil. Later, in a time of peace, a basilica was built there.

Also, the feast of Saint Gaudentia the virgin with three others.

And the deposition of Agilus the abbot.

### E. The day before the Kalends of September

At Trier, the feast of Saint Paulinus the bishop and confessor. During the Arian persecution, he was banished into exile by the emperor Constantine because of the Catholic faith. He was worn out by repeated exiles, being transferred from place to place until death, even beyond the bounds of the Christian world.

[Col. 1027A]

At last he died in Phrygia and received from the Lord the crown of a blessed passion.

[Col. 1028A]

At Athens, the blessed Aristides the confessor.

### September

It has thirty days and the moon has thirty days.

[Col. 1027C]

### F. Kalends of September

The feast of blessed Anna the prophetess, daughter of Phanuel from the tribe of Asher, concerning whom the Evangelists speak; of Jesus son of Nave and Gideon, the prophets [a corrupt or misplaced printed fragment].

At Capua, the feast of Saint Priscus the martyr, who was one of those ancient disciples of Christ.

At Sens, the blessed Lupus the bishop, distinguished in holiness, and the blessed Longinus the martyr.

At the city of Scinomannis in Gaul, the feast of Victor the bishop.

When Saint Martin, bishop of Tours, was traveling to bury Leporinus, [Col. 1028C] bishop of the aforementioned city, and had come to the town, he looked around and saw a man working in a vineyard. He was a subdeacon, and it was revealed to the holy man of God that this man would succeed to the episcopal office.

Saint Martin called him to himself and said: “Bless, Lord Victor.”

He replied: “Bless me, my lord, and blessed be your word.”

Thus, by order of the holy man, he followed him. After summoning the people, Martin ordained him bishop. He baptized Victor’s son, named Victorinus, and took him with him to be brought up in the service of God. After the father’s death, he also ordained Victorinus bishop of that same city.

[Col. 1029A]

At Aquae Durae, the feast of Saint Verena the virgin, and of Saint Giles the abbot and confessor.

### G. Fourth day before the Nones of September

The feast of Saint Justus, bishop of Lyons, a man of extraordinary holiness and prophetic spirit. Secretly abandoning his episcopate, he boarded a ship accompanied by only one boy, a lector named Viator.

[Col. 1030A]

He reached Egypt, where for several years he lived among holy monks who awaited heaven alone, practicing no ordinary humility and holiness.

When the course of time had been completed, he departed to the Lord, destined to receive the crown of righteousness, on the day before the Ides of October.

His body, together with the bones of the blessed Viator, his attendant, was brought back to Lyons by devout citizens and buried with fitting honor in the basilica of the holy Maccabees.

[Col. 1031A]

This took place on the fourth day before the Nones of September.

Also, in the aforementioned city, the blessed Elpidius the bishop and confessor.

At Apamea, Saint Antoninus the martyr.

### A. Third day before the Nones of September

The feast of Saint Phoebe, of whom the blessed Apostle writes to the Romans.

At Rome, the Passion of Saint Serapia the virgin, under the emperor Hadrian and the judge Beryllus. She was of Antiochene origin, and while living in the house of Sabina she was brought before the governor.

He said to her: “Sacrifice to the gods.”

She replied: “I fear and worship God almighty; I do not sacrifice to demons.”

The governor then ordered her to be handed over to five lustful young men, so that they might assault her by night. When they had brought her into a very dark room and wished to touch her, suddenly a great earthquake occurred.

[Col. 1032A]

They fell lifeless to the ground, all their limbs dislocated.

After this, the governor ordered her to be beaten with clubs and burning lamps to be applied to her sides, but those holding them fell backward. Then he ordered her to be struck with the sword.

She suffered on the fourth day before the Kalends of August and was buried by the blessed Sabina on the day before the Kalends of August. There, on the third day before the Nones of September, a venerable sarcophagus for both women was arranged and adorned, and a place of prayer was appropriately dedicated.

At Capua, the holy martyrs Antoninus, a twenty-year-old boy, and Aristaeus the bishop, whose acts are preserved.

### B. The day before the Nones of September

Of Moses the prophet.

At Ancyra in Galatia, the holy martyrs, three children: Rufinus, Silvanus, and Vitalica.

[Col. 1033A]

At Chalon, the feast of Saint Marcellus. Under the emperor Antoninus, he suffered before the governor Priscus, whom he confronted while the governor was sacrificing to his gods.

When he had been invited by Priscus to a profane banquet and, abhorring such fare, rebuked all who were present with free speech for serving idols, the governor ordered him, in an unheard-of act of cruelty, to be buried upright up to the waist.

Thus the holy martyr of God remained for three days praising almighty God and gave back his undefiled spirit.

### G. Nones of September

In the suburb of Rome, the blessed Victorinus the martyr. While leading the life of a hermit, he fell through the devil’s persuasion, but by God’s grace was restored. Later he attained the priesthood of the city of Amiternum.

[Col. 1034A]

Afterward, under the emperor Nerva, he was first banished by the judge Aurelian, together with other servants of God, Eutyches and Maronas, to the place where foul and sulfurous waters flow. There he was ordered by the impious judge to be suspended head downward for three hours and held there.

After suffering for three days for the name of Christ, he departed victoriously to the Lord, gloriously crowned. The people of Amiternum seized his body and buried it with an honored burial.

At Rome, Saint Herculanus the martyr.

At Capua, Saints Quintus, Arcontius, Donatus, Taurinus, Nymphus, and Saturninus, and the deposition of Ingenius the bishop.

### D. Eighth day before the Ides of September

Of Zachariah the prophet.

Also, the feast of the blessed Onesiphorus, a disciple of the apostles, concerning whom the Apostle says: “May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus.”

[Col. 1035A]

In Africa, the blessed confessors and bishops Donatianus, Praesidius, Mansuetus, Germanus, and Fusculus. During the Vandal persecution, by order of Huneric, the Arian king, they were brutally beaten with clubs and condemned to exile for asserting the Catholic truth.

Among them, he also burned in a fire a bishop named Laetus. At that time, when the bishops had been gathered at Carthage as though for a council, he closed all the churches of Africa on a single day and granted all the possessions of the bishops and churches to his own bishops.

Saint Magnus the confessor, a disciple of Saint Gall.

[Col. 1036A]

At Rome, Eleutherius the bishop.

At the city of Cappadocia, Saint Cuttidus the bishop, and Eugenius and his companions.

### D. Seventh day before the Ides of September

At Nicomedia, the feast of the blessed John under the emperor Diocletian. Although his entrails had already been exhausted by the tortures, they could never bring it about that anyone should see him sweating amid his punishments.

Also, the feast of Saint Euritius the bishop and confessor, and the deposition of Clodoaldus the confessor.

At Arles, Saint Augustalis the bishop and confessor, and Saint Regina the martyr.

[Col. 1037A]

### F. Sixth day before the Ides of September

The Nativity of Mary, the most blessed Mother of God, ever-virgin.

At Nicomedia, the feast of Saint Adrian the martyr with twenty-three others. After innumerable tortures, Maximian ordered their legs to be shattered with a great iron bar.

When their legs had been broken and their feet cut, Saint Adrian’s hand was also cut off. While praying and giving thanks to God, they gave up their spirit.

The tyrant ordered their bodies to be burned. But suddenly flashes of lightning, thunder, and rain arose, and the fire was extinguished. Then Christians seized the martyrs’ relics, boarded ships, and fled to Byzantium, where they buried them with reverent honor.

Not long afterward, the body of Saint Adrian was transferred to Rome.

In the suburbs of the church of Mainz, the feast of [Col. 1037B] Saint Disibod the confessor; and at Freising, the deposition of Saint Corbinianus the bishop.

### G. Fifth day before the Ides of September

Of Sergius the pope, who sat at Rome for thirteen years.

[Col. 1038A]

He discovered in the shrine of blessed Peter a piece of the saving wood of the Lord’s cross, of extraordinary size.

He decreed that, at the time of the breaking of the Lord’s body, the *Agnus Dei* should be sung by clergy and people. He also established that on the days of the Annunciation of the Lord, the Dormition and Nativity of the holy Mother of God Mary, and Saint Simeon’s feast—which is called *Hypapante* in Greek—the litanies should go out from Saint Hadrian’s, and the people should meet at Saint Mary’s.

The Passion of the blessed martyrs Dorotheus and Gorgonius.

At Nicomedia, under the emperor Diocletian, they were ordered to be hung and their entire bodies torn with scourges. When their entrails had been laid bare by the stripping of their skin, vinegar and salt were poured over them.

After this, a grating covered with burning coals was ordered to be placed in the middle, and what remained of the consumed man was placed upon it. He ordered it to be burned not [Col. 1038B] suddenly but gradually. Finally, he ordered him to be killed by hanging him from a noose.

After some time, the blessed Gorgonius was transferred to Rome.

In the Sabine territory, Saints Hyacinthus, Alexander, and Tiburtius.

[Col. 1039A]

On the same day, Saint Cunegund the virgin.

### A. Fourth day before the Ides of September

In Africa, the holy bishops Nemesianus and Felix; also Felix, Litteus, Polianus, Victor, Jader, and Datius, who suffered under Diocletian and Maximian.

At Chalcedon, the holy martyrs Sosthenes and Victurius, under the consul Priscus.

At Rome, the deposition of Hilary the pope, through whom Victurius wrote the paschal cycle.

[Col. 1040A]

And the deposition of Salvius the bishop. Gregory, bishop of Tours, wrote about his holiness, recounting that in a revelation he saw a sword drawn by a divine voice hanging over the roof that King Chilperic had ordered to be built. The truth of the vision followed immediately: twenty-two days later, the king’s sons died.

[Col. 1041A]

### B. Third day before the Ides of September

At Rome, the feast of Saints Protus and Hyacinthus, who were eunuchs of the blessed virgin Eugenia.

After being baptized by Bishop Helenus, they devoted themselves for some time solely to divine instruction and lived with extraordinary humility in a monastery of servants of God, in Egypt. Then they returned to Rome with the blessed virgin.

Under the emperor Gallienus, when they were discovered to be Christians, they were compelled to sacrifice. Since they refused, they were cruelly beaten. Rejoicing while maintaining faith in God, they were beheaded together.

And the feast of Saints Felix and Regula.

### C. The day before the Ides of September

Near the city of Ticinum, also called Pavia, the holy confessors Syrus and [Col. 1042A] Juventius. They were sent to that city by the blessed Hermagoras, bishop of Aquileia and disciple of Saint Mark the Evangelist.

There they first preached the Gospel of Christ and shone with great virtues and miracles. They also enlightened the neighboring cities—Verona, Brixen, and Lodi—with divine works. Thus, after the faith of the believing peoples had been founded and confirmed, they rested in peace with a glorious end in the honor of the episcopate.

At Antioch, the feast of Timothy.

The chains of Saint Euplus.

At Lyons, the deposition of Sacerdos the bishop.

At Autun, the blessed Eventius the bishop.

### D. Ides of September

At Alexandria, the blessed Philip the bishop and martyr. He was first a prefect, [Col. 1043A] but afterward, sanctified by the grace of baptism, he attained the dignity of the episcopate with the support of the Christian people.

Under the emperors Volusian and Gallienus, Perhemius, prefect of Alexandria, planned to kill him. But since he could not accomplish this because of the Christian people, he sent men who pretended to be Christians. They entered and struck him while he was at prayer.

He sat in the episcopate for one year and three months.

Also, Saint Amatus the presbyter and abbot of the monastery of Saint Romaricus.

At Tours, the deposition of the blessed Licerius the bishop.

### E. Eighteenth day before the Kalends of October

At Rome, on the Appian Way, the feast of Saint Cornelius the bishop during the persecution of Decius. First his mouth was beaten with leaded scourges, and then he was beheaded [Col. 1043B] with twenty-one others, men and women alike. Among them were also Cerealis the soldier and his wife Salustia, whom Cornelius [Col. 1044A] healed from illness by praying.

The blessed Cornelius, at the request of the blessed Lucina, secretly lifted up by night the bodies of the apostles Peter and Paul from the catacombs.

First, the blessed Lucina took the body of Saint Paul and placed it on her estate on the Ostian Way, beside the place where he had been beheaded. Saint Cornelius, the bishop, took the body of Saint Peter and placed it near the place where he had been crucified, among the bodies of the saints, in the temple of Apollo on Mount Aurelius of the Vatican palace of Nero, on the third day before the Kalends of July.

Also, Saint Cyprian the bishop, who under the emperor Valerian, after a long exile, completed his martyrdom by being beheaded, six miles from Carthage beside the sea.

On the same day, the Exaltation of the Holy Cross.

At Trier, the deposition of Saint Maternus the bishop and confessor.

[Col. 1044B]

### F. Seventeenth day before the Kalends of October

The feast of Saint Nicomedes the martyr. Because he had buried the body of the holy [Col. 1045A] virgin Felicula, whom Flaccus the count had punished for Christ, Flaccus ordered Nicomedes to be taken away for sacrifice.

When he refused, he was beaten for a very long time with leaded scourges and departed to the Lord. His body was thrown into the Tiber, but it was recovered by his cleric, named Justus, and buried beside the walls on the Nomentan Way.

At the fortress of Chalon, at Trenorcium, Saint Valerian the martyr. Under the governor Priscus, he was ordered to be suspended, tortured with the grievous tearing of hooks, and then struck with the sword.

Also, the feast of Saint Aper the bishop and Saint Leobinus the confessor.

At Alexandria, Saints Serapion and Leontius.

At Cyra in Galatia, Saints Eleucus, Valerius, Cyrion, Strato, Macrobius, and Constantius.

At Ancyra, Saint Paul the bishop.

At Lyons, the deposition of Albinus the bishop, and the octave of the feast of Saint Mary the virgin.

[Col. 1045B]

### G. Sixteenth day before the Kalends of October

The feast of Saint Euphemia the virgin, who was martyred under the emperor Diocletian, with Priscus as proconsul, in the city of Chalcedon.

She overcame tortures and prisons, beatings and devices, [Col. 1046A] the mechanisms of wheels, fires and weights of cornerstones, beasts and blows from rods, sharp saws, and heated frying pans.

At last the holy virgin obtained by her prayers that one of the beasts should bite her. Thus she gave her undefiled spirit back to the Lord.

Her father Philophronus and her mother Theodora tended and buried her body about a thousand paces from the city of Chalcedon.

At Rome, Saints Lucia and Geminianus, under the emperor Diocletian, with Apofrasius and Megasius as judges.

The blessed Lucia had remained a widow for thirty-six years; the whole span of her life was seventy-five years. Accused by her son of living as a Christian, she was first sent to prison, where she earned divine consolation.

Then she was beaten for a very long time with clubs, and suddenly a great earthquake occurred. [Col. 1046B] The temple of Jupiter was so overturned that not one stone remained upon another.

Then she was put into a bronze cauldron boiling with pitch and lead, where she remained unharmed for three days.

Afterward, loaded with lead and iron [Col. 1047A] and dragged through the streets of the city, she was seen by a certain man named Geminianus. He saw heaven opened for him, and immediately joined Saint Lucia in prison. There, at the angel’s instruction, he was baptized by a presbyter named Prothasius.

Then Saint Lucia and Geminianus were brought before the consul Amegas. Finally, they were put to death by the sword.

A Christian woman named Maxima seized their bodies and buried them as was fitting.

### A. Fifteenth day before the Kalends of October

In the diocese of Tongeren, at Liège, a public estate, the feast of Saint Lambert the bishop. When he had rebuked the royal household with religious zeal, he returned and devoted himself to prayer. Then the most wicked men sent from the royal palace unexpectedly surrounded him within the church building and killed him.

His tomb is made illustrious by very frequent miracles.

In Britain, Socrates [Col. 1047B] and Stephen.

At Nevers, Saints Valerian, Macrinus, and Gordianus.

At Rome, the blessed Justin the presbyter, whom the blessed Sixtus ordained. He buried the blessed martyrs Lawrence, Hippolytus, Concordia, Irenaeus, Abundius, and Cyrilla, the daughter of Caesar Decius, together with many others.

Also at Rome, the holy martyrs Narcissus and Crescention.

### B. Fourteenth day before the Kalends of October

The feast of Saint Methodius, Olympius, and Lucius; Methodius later became bishop of Tyre and was crowned with martyrdom at Chalcis in Greece under Diocletian [Col. 1048A].

At Vienne, Saint Ferreolus. During the persecution, while holding tribunician authority, he was first seized by order of the governor and cruelly beaten. Then, weighed down by heavy chains, he was thrust into a most dreadful prison.

Freed by God’s will, he was later captured by those pursuing him and received the palm of martyrdom by being beheaded. His body, together with the head of the blessed Julian, was brought to the city of Vienne and buried with fitting honor.

At Milan, the deposition of the blessed Eustorgius the bishop, and of Satyrus, Theophimus, and Jocianus.

### C. Thirteenth day before the Kalends of October

At Naples in Campania, the feast of the holy Januarius, bishop of Benevento, with Sosius, deacon of Misenum, his own deacon Festus, and his lector Desiderius.

After [Col. 1048B] chains and imprisonments, they were beheaded at the city of Pozzuoli under the emperor Diocletian and the judge Dracontius.

As they were being led to execution, they saw among the others Proculus, deacon of Pozzuoli, and two laymen, Eutyches and Acacius. They asked why just men were ordered to be killed.

When the judge saw that they were Christians, he ordered them to be beheaded with the others. Thus all seven were beheaded together, and Christian people took away their bodies by night.

The Neapolitans placed Januarius beside the city in a basilica. The people of Misenum likewise placed Sosius in a basilica. The people of Pozzuoli placed Proculus, Eutyches, and Acacius beside the basilica of Saint Stephen. The people of Benevento gathered Festus and Desiderius.

[Col. 1049A]

In Palestine, Saints Peleus and Nilus, bishops, who during the persecution of Diocletian were burned for Christ with many clerics.

At Nuceria, Saints Felix and Constantia, who suffered under Nero.

At Langres, Sigonius the presbyter, and Florentius the bishop and martyr.

And the feast of Saint Eustochius.

### D. Twelfth day before the Kalends of October

At Cyzicus, the feast of Fausta the virgin and Evilasius under the emperor Maximian.

Evilasius, who was chief of the palace, ordered Fausta to have her hair cut off and her head shaved to disgrace her, and then to be suspended and tortured.

At that time a flash of lightning from heaven struck many [Col. 1049B] of the attendants.

Then he ordered small coffins to be brought. Fausta was put into one and fastened in place, as though she were a piece of wood, and ordered to be sawn in two. But the executioners could not harm her with their instruments.

Evilasius, astonished by these things, began to believe in Christ. When this was reported to the emperor, he sent the prefect, [Col. 1050A] who had Evilasius suspended and fiercely tortured.

The prefect also ordered Fausta to be stripped naked, scourged without a cloak, imprisoned, her head pierced, and her eyes pierced through. Later not only her head and face but also her breast and entire body down to her shins were filled with nails.

After this he ordered a frying pan to be heated, but while she sang psalms it grew cold.

Then a voice from heaven intervened and called them. Thus they gave up their spirit.

Fausta was thirteen years old, and Evilasius eighty.

And the vigil of Saint Matthew the apostle.

### E. Eleventh day before the Kalends of October

The feast of Saint Matthew the apostle and evangelist, who first wrote the Gospel of Christ in Judea in the Hebrew language.

Afterward he preached in Ethiopia and converted many to the faith. Hirtacus the king sent an executioner, [Col. 1050B] who struck him with the sword and made him a martyr of Christ.

His Gospel, written by a stylus, was discovered in the time of a certain emperor, with the Hebrew author himself revealing it.

### F. Tenth day before the Kalends of October

In Gaul, at the city of Octodurum, in the place called Agaunum, the feast of the holy Theban martyrs [Col. 1051A] Maurice, Candidus, Exuperius, Victor, Innocent, and Vitalis with their companions—namely, 6,666 men—who suffered under Maximian and were gloriously crowned for Christ.

Victor the martyr, however, belonged neither to the same legion nor was he a soldier; he was a veteran who had already completed his military service.

While traveling, he came upon these men, who were joyfully feasting everywhere upon the spoils of the martyrs. They invited him to eat with them. When he learned in order the reason for their celebration, he detested the feasters and withdrew.

They immediately seized and slaughtered him, and he was joined in honor to the other martyrs.

After many years had passed since their Passion, the bodies of the most blessed martyrs were revealed to Saint Theodore the bishop, and a basilica was honorably built and furnished in their honor.

At Regensburg, the blessed [Col. 1051B] Emmeram the bishop and martyr, whose limbs were individually cut off.

### G. Ninth day before the Kalends of October

The feast of Saint Sosius, deacon of the city of Misenum in Campania. When he was thirty years old, he suffered beheading together with the blessed Januarius, bishop of Benevento, [Col. 1052A] in the time of the emperor Diocletian.

Once, while he was reading the Gospel in the church of Misenum in the presence of Bishop Januarius—for the bishop frequently visited him because of his holiness and wisdom—the bishop suddenly saw a flame rise from Sosius’s head. No one else saw it. Januarius declared that Sosius would become a martyr.

Not many days afterward the deacon was seized and sent to prison. When the bishop came to visit him with the deacon Festus and his lector Desiderius, the bishop himself was also seized with them. All were killed together with three others.

On the same day, the feast of Saint Thecla the virgin, from the city of Iconium, who was instructed by the blessed apostle Paul.

Under the emperor Nero she was handed over to fire [Col. 1052B] for the name of Christ, but was not burned. Later she was assigned to beasts and serpents, but none of them harmed her. Finally, at Seleucia, she departed to the Lord in the sleep of peace, bearing the double crown of virginity and martyrdom.

The second Assumption of Saint Mary the virgin.

[Col. 1053A]

### A. Eighth day before the Kalends of October

The Conception of Saint John the Baptist.

At Autun, the feast of Andochius the presbyter, Thyrsus the deacon, and Felix, who had been sent from the East by Saint Polycarp the bishop to teach Gaul. Under the emperor Aurelian they were gloriously crowned.

They were beaten with scourges, then finally suspended all day with their hands bound behind them, and thrown into the fire, but were not burned. At last their necks were struck with bars, and thus they completed their martyrdom.

On the same day, the deposition of Bishop Solemnis. One day, when he met a man blind and deaf from birth, he embraced him by the neck and kissed him, and immediately restored him to health.

He was also bishop of the Carnutes, and regenerated King Louis together with 370 nobles in the sacred font. Thus, after serving three Olympiads in the episcopate, the holy man departed to the Lord.

[Col. 1054A]

At Rome, Priscilla, and Liberius the bishop and confessor.

At Clermont, the deposition of Rusticus the bishop and Saint Rupert the confessor.

### B. Seventh day before the Kalends of October

The feast of the blessed Cleopas, who was one of the seventy disciples of Christ. After the Resurrection, the Lord appeared to him as he was going with another fellow disciple to the village of Emmaus, which is now called Nicopolis.

They relate that Cleopas was killed by the Jews in that same city and in the same house where he had prepared a table for the Lord as for a stranger, because he confessed the one whom he himself had recognized there. He was buried there also in glorious memory.

At Lyons, Saint Lupus the bishop, one of the anchorites, and the feast of Saint Firminus the martyr.

In Asia, Bardomianus, Eucarpius, and twenty-six others.

### C. Sixth day before the Kalends of October

The feast of the holy martyrs Cyprian the bishop and Justina the virgin.

Under Diocletian, Justina suffered many things for Christ. She converted Cyprian himself to Christ, although he was a magician and was attempting to drive her mad by magical arts.

After he had become a bishop and distinguished teacher, she was martyred with him under the emperor Claudius and the judge Eutellius, together with a certain Theognitus.

[Col. 1055A]

Their bodies lay cast outside unburied for six days. Then certain Christian sailors took them away by night and carried them to the city of Rome. The venerable matron Rufina received them reverently and buried them on her estate.

[Col. 1056A]

### D. Fifth day before the Kalends of October

At the city of Aegae, the feast of the holy martyrs Cosmas and Damian, during the persecution of Diocletian and under the governor Lysias.

After enduring many tortures, chains, and imprisonments, as well as sea and fire, crosses, stonings, and arrows, they were beheaded together with Anthimus, Leontius, and Euprepius.

Religious men buried their bodies in a venerable place not far from the city of Aegae. The memory of the two brothers Cosmas and Damian is also solemnly celebrated in a splendid temple built in their name.

### E. Fourth day before the Kalends of October

In Spain, at the city of Córdoba, [Col. 1057A] the feast of the holy Faustus, Januarius, and Martialis.

They were first tortured by the punishment of the rack. Then their eyebrows were shaved, their ears and noses cut off, and their upper teeth pulled out, so that they were disfigured. Finally, they completed their martyrdom by the torture of fire.

In Germany, Saint Lioba the virgin, who was summoned from the island of Britain by Saint Boniface, archbishop of the Church of Mainz, to instruct the handmaids of God in the monasteries of Germany in the divine Scriptures.

While alive she performed many miracles; indeed, after her death she continued to shine with numerous miracles. She was buried, according to Saint Boniface’s decree, in the monastery of Fulda in the forest of Buchonia.

On the same day, the Passion of Saint Wenceslaus the martyr.

At Rome, the feast of Sterteus.

In Africa, Martialis, Laurentius, and twenty others.

At Auxerre, the deposition of Saint Alodius the bishop, and in Gaul, of Solornus the bishop.

[Col. 1057B]

### F. Third day before the Kalends of October

On Mount Garganus, the venerable memorial of the blessed archangel Michael, where there is a church consecrated in his name. It was built in a humble form but endowed with heavenly power.

Situated at the summit of a lofty mountain, it appears to be a cave hollowed out of the body of the same [Col. 1058A] rock.

When the Roman pontiff and the bishop of Sipontum were inquiring about the consecration of this place, and were therefore observing a three-day fast with the citizens, on the final night of the fast Saint Michael appeared in a vision to the bishop of Sipontum and instructed him to enter the church that he himself had dedicated and celebrate Masses there according to custom.

Countless benefits are also bestowed there through the merits of the holy archangels.

At the city of Heraclea in Thrace, the feast of Eutychus and Platus.

At Auxerre, the deposition of Fraternus the bishop.

### G. The day before the Kalends of October

At Bethlehem in Judea, the deposition of Saint Jerome the presbyter. His life and teaching remain praiseworthy everywhere in the churches of Christ. He translated the divine books from the Hebrew language into [Col. 1058B] Latin and explained the prophetic books in an allegorical sense.

At last, after a life pleasing to God, he rested in peace at Bethlehem in the ninety-eighth year of his age, in the twelfth year of the emperor Honorius.

In Gaul, at the fortress of Solodurum, the holy martyrs Victor and Ursus, from the glorious Theban Legion.

[Col. 1059A]

By order of the tyrant Maximian, they were first tortured by severe punishments at the hands of the executioner Hirtacus. But when heavenly light flashed over them, the attendants fell to the ground and the martyrs were rescued.

Then they were thrown into the fire, but soon a violent rain came and extinguished the pyre; they were not harmed in the least.

[Col. 1060A]

Finally, they were brought to completion by the sword.

### October

It has thirty days and the moon has twenty-eight days.

[Col. 1059B]

A. **Kalends of October**.—At Auxerre, the feast of Saint Germanus, bishop and confessor, who was distinguished by many virtues, learning, and continence. At Reims, Saint Remigius, bishop and confessor, a man of outstanding virtue and holiness. He converted the Frankish people, devoted to the worship of idols, to Christ, after first initiating their king into the sacred font of baptism and the sacraments of the faith. He completed more than seventy years in the episcopate. [Col. 1060B] Among his other deeds, he raised a girl from bodily death. At Trier, Saint Nicetius, bishop and confessor, who was holy from his mother’s womb. For from the very time of his birth he was miraculously marked out as a cleric. When he had been delivered at birth, he emerged with his entire head bare of hair, as is customary among newborns, except that a small orderly ring of hair appeared around it. At Arras, the blessed Vedast, bishop and confessor, and Babo, bishop. Also Saint Fronto, bishop, whose deeds, full of miracles, are preserved in writing. At Tomi, the feast of Saints Priscus, Crescentius, and Evagrius.

[Col. 1061A]

B. **Sixth day before the Nones of October**.—The feast of Saint Eusebius, pope, who sat in the episcopate for seven years and was buried on the Appian Way, in the cemetery of Callistus. During his pontificate the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ was discovered, on the fifth day before the Nones of May. He found heretics in the city and reconciled them through the laying on of hands. In the territory of Arras, at the estate of Syricinium, the passion of Saint Leodegarius, bishop of Autun, whom Hebroinus, mayor of the royal palace, killed after he had been afflicted with various insults and diverse tortures for the sake of the truth. His most sacred body was transferred to the diocese of Poitiers and honorably buried in the monastery of the blessed Maxentius. At Nicomedia, Saint Eleutherius, martyr, who, under Diocletian, after being tested by various kinds of tortures, [Col. 1062A] departed to Christ.

C. **Fifth day before the Nones of October**.—The feast of Saint Dionysius the Areopagite, who, instructed by the Apostle Paul, believed in Christ and was ordained by that same apostle as the first bishop of Athens. Under the emperor Hadrian, after a most illustrious confession of faith and extremely severe kinds of torture, he was crowned with glorious martyrdom. Among the ancient Saxons, the feast of the two holy Evalds, priests, who came into Germany with the blessed bishop Willibrord and proceeded to the Saxons. When they had begun to preach Christ there, they were seized and killed by the pagans. A great light appeared by night for a long time at their bodies, revealing both where they were and what merit they possessed.

[Col. 1063A]

D. **Fourth day before the Nones of October**.—At Corinth, the blessed Crispus and Gaius, whom the blessed Apostle says he baptized; he mentions this Gaius in Romans: “Gaius, my host,” he says, “greets you, and that of the whole Church.” The blessed John also mentions him when writing his Epistle, in this manner: “The elder to the most beloved Gaius, whom I love in truth.” In Egypt, Saints Mark and Martian, martyrs and brothers, and with them innumerable others, men and women of no lesser glory, as well as children and old people, who, for the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, regarding the present life as of little account, sought the blessedness of future glory. Some of them, after scourging and other horrible tortures of various kinds, were handed over to the flames; others were thrown into the sea; some were consumed by hunger; others were fastened to gibbets; [Col. 1063B] and some were beheaded, so that they willingly offered their necks to the axes. Among them, some, in a perverse manner, with their heads pressed downward and their feet raised aloft, earned the most blessed crown of passion. [Col. 1064A] In Africa, Audactus; at Rome, Pope Marcellus; at Auxerre, the deposition of Marsus, priest. On the same day, Saint Francis, confessor.

E. **Third day before the Nones of January**.—In Sicily, the feast of Saints Placidus, Eutychius, and thirty others. In Gaul, at the city of Valence, the feast of Saint Apollinaris, bishop, whose life was distinguished by its virtue, and whose death likewise was adorned with signs and wonders. At Eumenia, the blessed Praseas, bishop, who was brought to completion by martyrdom at Smyrna and who, as one of the ancients, claimed to have received by tradition from his predecessors that the Savior had commanded his apostles not to depart from Jerusalem before the twelfth year. At Auxerre, the deposition of Saints Germanus and Firmatus, deacon, and Flavina, a virgin consecrated to God.

[Col. 1064B]

F. **Day before the Nones of October**.—At Capua, the feast of Saints Marcellus, Castus, Aemilius, and Saturninus. In Gaul, at the city of Agaunum, the feast of Faith, virgin and martyr, whose example encouraged the blessed Caprasius to the contest of martyrdom. [Col. 1065A] On the same day, the blessed Sagarus, martyr and bishop of Laodicea, who was one of the ancient disciples of the Apostle Paul. The deposition of Romanus, bishop of Auxerre. On the same day, the octave of Saint Michael the Archangel.

G. **Nones of October**.—At Rome, on the Appian Way, the feast of Saint Mark, bishop and confessor, who sat in the episcopate for two years, nine months, and twenty days. He was also buried in the cemetery of Balbina on the Ardeatine Way. Also Saints Sergius and Bacchus, martyrs, who suffered for Christ under Maximian. Sergius was chief officer of the school of the pagans and a friend of the emperor, while the blessed Bacchus was second officer of that same school. They suffered for Christ under Antiochus the commander, by order of the emperor Maximian. [Col. 1065B] Bacchus, while stretched out and beaten with scourges on the cross, gave up his spirit; Sergius, after many tortures, was struck with the sword and thus departed to [Col. 1066A] the Lord. Also Saints Marcellus and Apuleius, martyrs, who at first adhered to Simon Magus; but when they saw the wonders that the Lord performed through his apostle Peter, they abandoned Simon, devoted themselves to apostolic teaching, and, after the martyrdom of the apostles, completed their crown of martyrdom under the consul Aurelian. They were buried not far from the city of Rome.

A. **Eighth day before the Ides of October**.—The feast of the blessed Simeon, who presented our Lord Jesus Christ in the Temple. Also the feast of Saint Reparata, virgin, who suffered in the city of Caesarea in Palestine under the governor Decius. Because she refused to sacrifice to idols, a pot filled with boiling lead was first brought against her; afterward her breasts were cut off, and burning lamps were applied; [Col. 1066B] then she was thrown into a furnace. Since she was not harmed there in any way, she was beheaded, and immediately a white dove came forth from her neck. Christians carried away her body, embalmed it with spices, and buried it. [Col. 1067A] In Crete, at the city of Cortyna, the blessed Philip, bishop. At Thessalonica, Saints Demetrius and Pelagia. On the same day, Saint Amor, confessor.

B. **Seventh day before the Ides of October**.—Abraham the patriarch. At Paris, the feast of Saints Dionysius, bishop, Eleutherius, priest, and Rusticus, deacon, martyrs. The blessed bishop had been sent into Gaul by Pope Clement of Rome to devote himself to preaching among peoples alienated from the faith of Christ. At length he came to the city of Paris and, after faithfully and zealously carrying out the holy work for several years, was seized by the prefect Fescenninus Sisinnius. With him, the holy priest Eleutherius and Rusticus the deacon were executed by the sword and completed their martyrdom. Also Saint Doninus, who was beheaded for the faith of Christ under the emperor Maximian.

[Col. 1067B] [Col. 1068A]

C. **Sixth day before the Ides of October**.—Lot the prophet. At Cologne, the feast of Saints Gereon and three hundred and eighteen other martyrs, who are said to have been Thebans and to have crossed into Gaul with that contingent of the blessed Maurice, at the command of the emperor Maximian. They settled near the banks of the Rhine and, rejecting the tyrant’s deadly rule, patiently submitted their necks to the swords for true devotion. In Crete, the blessed Pinitus, bishop. In Britain, the blessed Paulinus, bishop of York, who converted to the Lord by preaching [Col. 1068B] the word of faith the Northumbrian people—that is, the nation of the Angles who lived north of the river Humber—together with their king Edwin.

[Col. 1069A]

D. **Fifth day before the Ides of October**.—At Tarsus, the metropolis of Cilicia, the feast of Saints Tharacus, Probus, and Andronicus, who during the persecution of Diocletian, with Maximian as governor, were afflicted for a long time by the squalor of prison and were finally put to death by various tortures. They were severely beaten with raw sinews and rubbed with extremely rough potsherds; they were also burned around the belly and sides with flaming papyrus. After the crushing of their breasts, the torture of their shins, the pouring in of vinegar and mustard, the application of red-hot coins, the piercing of their fingers with extremely sharp nails, the piercing of their eyes, and the cutting out of their tongues, they were finally thrown to bears and lions in the amphitheater. But when none of the beasts dared touch the bodies of the saints, Maximian, inflamed with anger, ordered them to be slaughtered with the sword and their bodies thrown among the bodies of the gladiators. [Col. 1069B] At night the faithful came and begged the Lord to show them the relics of the saints. Suddenly they saw what appeared to be a bright star sent from heaven, resting over each of the saints’ bodies. Thus, with immense joy, they seized them; the radiance of that same star went before them, and they buried the glorious athletes of Christ in a most suitable place.

[Col. 1070A]

E. **Fourth day before the Ides of October**.—At Ravenna, on the Laurentian Way, the feast of Saint Edistus. In Africa, the holy confessors and martyrs, four thousand nine hundred and seventy-six in number, who, during the Vandal persecution, when they were bishops, priests, and deacons of the churches of God, accompanied by crowds of faithful peoples, were driven by order of Huneric, the Arian king, into a dreadful exile in the desert for defending Catholic truth and were assigned among the fiercest Moors. Among them were Cyprian and Felix, outstanding priests of the Lord. Many of them, while being cruelly led away, with spear-points attached to them so that they would run, and with stones tied to them while they were beaten, or with their feet bound and dragged like corpses through harsh and rugged places, were torn limb from limb by such atrocious punishment. [Col. 1070B] One man’s head was pierced by thongs (*loris*; uncertain), others had their sides split open by the sharp stones, and they breathed out their spirit in the hands of those dragging them. Throughout the entire public embankment there remains the burial of the saints, whose tombs speak. In Syria, Eustatius, priest, and Eucharistus, Burrus, Donatus, Fortunata.

E. **Third day before the Ides of October**.—The feast of Saint Carpus, disciple of [Col. 1071A] the Apostle Paul. At Troas, Theophilus of Antioch, who, as a most learned man, held the chief office of the Church as its sixth bishop after the apostles. In Spain, the feast of Faustinus, Marcus, and Adria. At Chalcedon, Marcellus. At Alexandria, the feast of Saint Anastasius, bishop, and Saint Lupentius, priest, and Saint Geraldus, confessor.

G. **Day before the Ides of October**.—The feast of Saint Callistus, pope, who sat in the episcopate for seven years, two months, and ten days. He established that fasting should be observed on Saturday three times a year, with wheat, wine, and oil, according to the prophecy. During the persecution of the emperor Alexander, he was tortured for a long time by hunger in prison and beaten daily with clubs. He was comforted in a vision by his priest Calepodius, who had previously completed his martyrdom. While Callistus was placed in the same prison, he cured a soldier named Privatus both of the pain and foulness of his ulcers and of unbelief. When Alexander heard this, he had the soldier beaten to death with leaded scourges; but he ordered the blessed Callistus to be thrown from a window of the house, sunk into a well with a stone fastened around his neck, and covered over with rubble. After fourteen days, his priest Asterius came by night with clerics, lifted the body, and buried it in the cemetery of Calepodius. At Córdoba, Saint Lupus of Aurelia. At Lyons in Gaul, the departure of Saint Justus into the desert. On the same day, the translation of Saint Burchard, bishop and confessor.

[Col. 1072A]

A. **Ides of October**.—In Gaul, at Cologne, [Col. 1073A] the holy Moors from among the soldiers, who, numbering three hundred and forty from that sacred Theban legion, completed their martyrdom at the same city and were buried in a basilica that shines, by its marvelous work in mosaic, as though gilded. Hence the inhabitants customarily call them “the golden saints.” At Vienne, Saints Agratius and Costor, bishops. At Capua, Libulus and Saint Fortunata.

B. **Seventeenth day before the Kalends of November**.—The deposition of Saint Gallus, confessor, whose life is preserved in writing as full of virtues. At Lyons, the blessed Antiochus, bishop. At Vienne, Saint Theodatus, bishop, and also Heron, who governed the Church of Antioch after the blessed Ignatius. He had been the deacon of the blessed martyr Ignatius; when he became bishop, he piously imitated the way of his teacher and, as a lover of Christ, died for the flock entrusted to him. In Gaul, at the city of Orange, Saint Florentius, bishop, who, distinguished by many virtues, rested in peace. At Nicomedia, Alexander. In Mauretania, Nina, Victorius, Nobilitanus, Marianus, Lucius, Mittinus, and Crescentianus, and Saint Eliphius, martyr.

[Col. 1074A]

C. **Sixteenth day before the Kalends of November**.—In Africa, two hundred and seventy martyrs crowned together, and the holy martyrs Martianus and Satyrnianus, with [Col. 1075A] their two brothers and the outstanding handmaid of Christ, Maxima the virgin. During the Vandal persecution under Genseric, the Arian king, they were first beaten with knotted clubs and torn to the bone for their steadfastness in the Catholic faith. Although they suffered such things for a long time, each following day they were found unharmed. Finally, with their feet tied behind the chariots of those driving them, they were ordered to perish together among thorny forest places. As the bodies of the innocent were torn by the prickles of the woody thickets while they were dragged forward and backward, they called out to one another as they ran nearby: “Brother, pray for me. God has fulfilled our desire; this is how one reaches the kingdom of heaven.” Thus, while they prayed and sang psalms and the angels rejoiced, they gave up their devout souls. Also the blessed Aristo, [Col. 1075B] who was one of the seventy disciples of Christ.

D. **Fifteenth day before the Kalends of November**.—The feast of Saint Luke the Evangelist, who was by nationality a Syrian, from Antioch, a physician by profession, a disciple of the apostles, and a follower of Paul until his confession. Serving the Lord without blame, he never had a wife or children, and died at the age of seventy-three in Bithynia, full of the Holy Spirit. He is now buried at Constantinople; in the twentieth year of Constantius, his bones were transferred to that city together with the relics of the Apostle Andrew. At Rome, Saint Tryphonia, wife of Caesar Decius, [Col. 1076A] who, after her husband had been divinely punished following the killing of the blessed Sixtus, Laurence, and Hippolytus, requested baptism with her daughter Cyrilla, the daughter of Decius, from the priest Justinus. She died the following day and was buried in a crypt beside Saint Hippolytus. Also Saint Asclepiades, bishop of Antioch.

E. **Fourteenth day before the Kalends of November**.—At Antioch in Syria, the feast of Saints Beronicus and Pelagia. She had first, under pagan custom, practiced prostitution and devoted herself to worldly enticements; afterward, through the grace of God and the teaching of Saint Nonnus, bishop, she was converted to the faith of Christ and baptized by that same bishop. She distributed all her property and possessions to the poor. Clothed in sackcloth and dressed in a cheap garment, she set out on pilgrimage and at [Col. 1076B] Jerusalem, in male clothing, led a monastic life. For she had built herself a small cell on the Mount of Olives, where the Lord ascended into heaven, and there she ended her present life and happily departed to eternal life.
