728. Again Charles was in Bavaria.

729.

730. Charles marched into Swabia against Lantfred.

[Col. 1177C] 731. Charles was in Wasconia against Eudo.

732. Charles fought against the Saracens in the month of October.

733. Charles came with an army to Wistragon.

734. Again Charles came with an army to Wistragon.

735. Charles was in Wasconia with an army.

736. Charles fought against the sons of Eudo.

737. Charles fought against the Saracens.

738.

739.

740.

741. Charles, duke of the Franks, died on the Ides of October.

742. Carloman led an army against Hunald.

743. Carloman entered into war against the Bavarians.

[Col. 1177D] 744.

745.

746.

747. Carloman marched to Rome.

748.

749. Grifo was in exile.

750.

751. Pippin was anointed king at Soissons.

752.

753. Hildegarius was killed in Saxony.

754. Pope Stephen came to Francia.

755. King Pippin marched into Italy with the Franks. He defeated the Lombards. Carloman died.

756.

757. The Franks besieged Pavia.

758. Pippin was in Saxony.

759.

[Col. 1178A] 760. King Pippin fought against Waifer.

761. Pippin was in Wasconia with Charles, and burned Clermont with fire.

762. Again Pippin, marching into Wasconia with Charles and Carloman, defeated the Vascones.

763. Pippin held an assembly at Worms. Then there was a most severe frost; it began on the 19th day before the Kalends of January and lasted until the 17th day before the Kalends of April.

764.

765. Pippin held an assembly at Attigny.

766. Pippin was in Wasconia and built Argentum.

767. Again Pippin was in Wasconia in the month of March, and again in the month of August.

768. Waifer was killed on the fourth day before the Nones of June, and King Pippin died on the eighth day before the Kalends of October; Charles and Carloman were anointed kings on the seventh day before the Ides of October.

[Col. 1178B] 769. King Charles was in Wasconia beyond the Garonne for the first time.

770.

771.

772. Carloman died at Samoussy on the day before the Nones of December.

773. King Charles fought against the Saxons at Heresburg.

774. King Charles was in Italy and fought against the Lombards.

775. Again Charles was in Italy; after capturing Desiderius, his wife, and his daughter, he brought them with him to Francia.

776. Again Charles was in Saxony, where he fought a battle and captured Sigiburg.

777. Again Charles was in Saxony; the Saxons were subjugated, and they gave hostages so that they might become Christians. Charles built a fortress above the River Lippe.

778. Charles held an assembly at Paderborn.

[Col. 1178C] 779. King Charles was in Spain, at Zaragoza.

780. King Charles divided his kingdoms among his sons and marched to Rome.

781.

782. The rebellious Saxons killed many Franks, and Charles ordered the Saxons, once assembled, to be beheaded. In this year Bishop Gislebert also died, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June.

783. Queen Hildegard died on the day before the Kalends of May, and Queen Bertrada, Charles’s mother, died at Choisy on the third day before the Ides of July.

784. Charles returned to Saxony three times and remained there.

785. Charles acquired Saxony, and Widukind was converted.

786. Charles ravaged the Thuringians because of their offenses.

787. Charles marched to Rome, and these signs appeared over the people.

[Col. 1178D] 788. Having captured Tassilo, Charles subjugated the Bavarians.

789. Charles fought against the Wiltzi in Wenedonia, and Charles, his son, received the kingdom beyond the Segona; and there was another most severe frost.

790.

791. King Charles was in Chunia for the first time.

792. The Saxons killed the Franks at the River Elbe near the sea, on the day before the Nones of July, on a Friday.

793.

794.

795.

796. King Charles sent his son Pippin into Chunia; when they received him peacefully, he took many treasures and brought them to Francia.

797. At Aachen, King Charles held a council with bishops, abbots, and monks from the monastery [Col. 1179A] of Saint Paul, concerning how he ought to establish it. In that same year he marched into Saxony and wintered there.

798. Charles wintered in Saxony, remained there throughout the summer, and brought back 1,600 chief hostages from there, distributing them throughout Francia.

799. The Romans condemned Pope Leo out of envy, and Leo himself came to Charles in Francia, and Charles restored him to his see.

800. King Charles was at the sea to fish; Queen Liutgard died; and he marched to Rome, reconciled the Romans and Pope Leo, and Leo blessed him as emperor.

801. Emperor Charles, returning from Rome, went back to Aachen. In that same year the Saracens came out, and were killed by the Franks.

802. Emperor Charles held a council at Aachen, so that all might swear allegiance to him generally—the monks and the canons; and so they did.

[Col. 1179B] 803.

804. Emperor Charles entered Saxony with his children and the Franks, and ordered some to be killed, [Col. 1180A] but others to be dispersed throughout his entire kingdom; and Pope Leo again came to Francia.

805. Emperor Charles sent his son Charles with an army into Wenedonia.

806. Emperor Charles divided his kingdom among his sons.

807. Emperor Charles held an assembly at Conflans with the Franks, and they gave their gifts, and returned to their own homes.

808. King Godefrid of the Normans came with an army into Wenedonia, and Emperor Charles sent his son Charles against him to resist him; and Godefrid returned to his own land.

809. In this year there was such a flood of waters as had never before been seen in this land, and it was at its highest on the fifth day before the Kalends of January. In this year the tomb of Saint Amandus, bishop, was raised on the twelfth day before the Kalends of October and restored to its place on the tenth day before the Kalends of November.

[Col. 1180B] 810. Emperor Charles marched with the Frankish army into Saxony, and held an assembly there at Verden; the Wends came there, and he gave them a king.
